2023 / Theatre, rehearsal and production archive
Breaking the Moon
A collaborative rehearsal process built around changing relationships between roles; directed by Xu Shuai, with He Fa credited as supervising producer.
Pre-performance poster, published in Breaking the Moon: Tickets Available on November 28, 2023. Full original layout and production credits preserved; no separate designer credit is given.
Image record & citation
hf-img-d1699da1d8f0
Breaking the Moon | Vertical Breaking the Moon poster and event text
The vertical poster combines a dark textured background with orange-red imagery and oversized white 破月 lettering down the right. The upper left lists 16 December at 7:30 pm, 321 Space and a price of 120 yuan. Writing, directing, producing and video-production credits gather below in a clear hierarchy of text.
He Fa’s role
Credited as supervising producer; performers describe his involvement in coordinating changes to the roles
Director and writer
Director: Xu Shuai; writer: Li Yaxin
Announced performance
December 16, 2023, 19:30–21:00, 321 Space, Beijing
Other production credits
Film/video production: Sun Jiarui; music: Zhao Ziyi; production coordination: Han Fengning; performance guidance: Jiujiu
Documented stage
Rehearsal accounts, production credits and pre-performance announcements, November–December 2023
From Burning the Moon to Breaking the Moon
In his signed article of November 27, 2023, He Fa introduced Xu Shuai’s new production. He explains that its earlier title, Burning the Moon, was changed to Breaking the Moon because another production used that name. His account describes rehearsals shaped by changing schedules and personnel, gradually connecting the participants, and invites readers to attend on December 16. The title change, rehearsals and performance plan are retained as stages of one production history.
The supervising producer within collaborative rehearsal
A performer’s account published on December 7 describes roles changing through rehearsal. One performer initially played an observer accompanying the others on a drum. As the group questioned the relationships and script, He Fa helped coordinate a new approach: the observer became a participant in the relationship between the other two performers. Improvisation continued from this revised framework. The account gives a concrete dimension to his supervising-producer credit while preserving the distinct contributions of director Xu Shuai, writer Li Yaxin and the performers.
Preserving the successive credits and announcements
Both the November 28 and December 7 credit lists name He Fa as supervising producer and Xu Shuai as director. The first lists Xueli, Wu Qiyou, Hou Xiaoxue and Zeilaman; the later list replaces the first name with Shanzha, without explaining the change. The December 7 announcement schedules a theatre salon at 321 Space for December 16, 19:30–21:00, with 30 audience places. These sources document rehearsals and production collaboration; the date, duration and capacity remain the terms of the pre-performance announcement.

sources.text:
2021 / P4U immersive theatre; associated writing
A Centrist’s Self-Rescue Guide After the Failure of Love
Audience choices enter a debate about love; He Fa responds through a signed text.
Poster announcing the 1 May 2021 performance; poster design credited to Gao Modi.
Image record & citation
hf-img-5527fc6c3380
Centrist’s Self-Rescue Guide: tiled text and purple lines
A vertical white poster combines gray cells, coloured letters, tiny photographs and dispersed Chinese characters. Thick purple curves loop through the grid. Broken-up title text sits between cells, with event information along the margins and varying density throughout.
He Fa’s role
Author of the signed announcement “Who Are the Centrists?”
Principal production credits
Director Chen Yu; writer Hu Junyuan; producer Zhang Shaohua; artistic adviser Tan Tian
Announced performance
1 May 2021, 19:30, P4 Theater
The production and He Fa’s writing
This P4U production explores romantic desire, rational restraint and choices within relationships. Its public introduction gives contrasting positions to different characters and makes audience choices part of the story’s direction. Actors and audiences share the space, and watching includes interaction and decision. The contemporary credits identify the responsibilities of Chen Yu, Hu Junyuan, Zhang Shaohua and other collaborators.
On the same day, He Fa published “Who Are the Centrists?”, using repetition, abrupt transitions and wordplay to create another narrative strand. His centrists wander, hesitate and wait to act; the closing passage returns the demand for a decision to the reader. Read beside the production introduction, the text shows how P4’s public writing participates in bringing a work into being: it communicates the schedule while establishing unsettled positions and emotions.
Role within this archive
This entry includes He Fa’s directly associated writing and preserves the production’s original credits. The poster, character dialogue and article together provide an entry into how the work was proposed within P4U’s framework of a single public performance.

2009 / Photography, light box
Inside and Outside a Vehicle
Streets, vehicles and windows repeat through several different image structures.
Inside and Outside a Vehicle, 2009. Portfolio image 1 of 4.
Image record & citation
hf-img-a28f62ea91ad
Repeated rows of traffic and a junction
Dense rows of small photographs repeat views of a road junction, cars, buses and pedestrians. White and yellow vehicles interrupt the gray roadway. Occasional foreground heads and shifted alignments break the otherwise regular traffic grid.
Artist
He Fa
Date
December 2009
Recorded dimensions
512 × 217 mm
Recorded medium
Light box
Images and presentation
Inside and Outside a Vehicle extends across four image pages in the portfolio. One image compresses roads, vehicles and buildings into repeated horizontal rows. Another sets night-time architecture alongside silhouettes of pedestrians. Elsewhere, regular window-like cells hold buses, roads and trees. Recognizable urban fragments recur without resolving into one continuous panorama.
The images can be compared through their different arrangements: some emphasize lateral extension, others retain the boundaries of individual frames, and colour alternates with monochrome. The portfolio gives no individual titles for the four images. Its title page records a light-box work measuring 512 × 217 mm, dated December 2009. All four images remain grouped under that title here.
Works & details
Inside and Outside a Vehicle, 2009. Portfolio image 2 of 4.

hf-img-ab8d3eac181d

A warm brown building rises above illuminated platform panels and waiting figures. Blue and violet ground areas fill the bottom. Walking people and parts of vehicles recur across adjacent photographs, separated by visible vertical montage seams.

hf-img-1b3f42f55504

Rows of black-bordered window views alternate pale foliage, distant buildings and objects near the frame. Branch angles and brightness vary between cells. Architectural outlines become clearer near the bottom, where thick borders separate each photographic observation.

chinesesamericandream / Instagram Thesis
“Fa He’s thesis is a instagram account.” A short statement redirects the reading of a thesis to a social platform account.

Artist’s statement identifying an account as a thesis
A thesis located in an account

The document moves the entry to a research project from a single text toward an account, a rhythm of posting and acts of browsing. The document metadata records creation on 10 May 2018 and modification on 12 May, with hefa as author. This site provides a readable transcription and retains the historical account link so the project can be read alongside Fafalish, YourTube and Fa’s review.

2020 / Dance theatre and collective production
Cocoon
Sixteen days and nights bring unfamiliar bodies, disagreements and shared work into the theatre.
Image accompanying the 2020 Cocoon backstage interviews.
Image record & citation
hf-img-22d49b2c9962
茧房｜人物侧面与墙上投影
A long-haired person in a blue-gray top stands sideways beside a pale wall, facing left. Warm directional light illuminates face and wall, casting a clear head-and-shoulder shadow to the right. Darkness borders the scene on the far left.
《茧房》项目文献配图：一名人物侧身站在浅色墙前，深色衣物与墙上的清晰侧影形成相邻的两个轮廓。作品关联据现存档案；拍摄日与具体场次未核实。
Copyright: P4 Theater
现存记录未单列逐图创作分工；本轮不补写
He Fa’s role
Production and organisational collaboration, signed writing and participation in backstage interviews
Director
Huang Yiyin
Production period
Rehearsals began 16 October 2020; performance on 31 October
How the work took shape
Cocoon is a dance-theatre work concerned with prejudice. Writing on 29 October 2020, He Fa records that director Huang Yiyin agreed the schedule with him and Zhang Shaohua in September. Recruitment began in early October, continuous rehearsals on the sixteenth, and the presentation followed at the end of the month. A production of nearly twenty people brought performers, dancers, lighting, documentation, publicity and audiences into a shared period of preparation. November’s backstage interviews continued the account through individual participants’ experiences.
Huang explains in the interviews that an initial concern with LGBTQ experiences developed into a broader inquiry into prejudice across genders and individuals. He Fa’s writing also records fatigue, lateness, physical strain, judgement and mutual support during production. This page preserves the work as both a performance and an event of working together: how bodies are seen, and how collaboration alters participants’ understanding of themselves.
He Fa’s writing at the time · 2020
“Theatre cannot happen only on the stage.” He Fa includes conversation, photography, argument and a passing glance among the conditions through which theatre happens. In the backstage interview, he stresses that differing roles do not prevent participants from expressing their views.

CLOSE READING / 2026 CURATORIAL INTERPRETATION
Cocoon
Whose bodies and time make the event possible?
Work date: 2020
Reading: 2026
Begin with what happens in the work
Rehearsal began on 16 October 2020, involving nearly twenty people; He Fa’s contemporary text describes the shared work.
Backstage interviews retain differing accounts of prejudice, bodies and collaboration from the director and participants.
This dance-theatre work cannot be understood only through attractive performance images. The contemporary text records repeated falls on a slippery stage, lateness, fatigue, injury, hunger and mutual judgments. These are not irrelevant matters outside creation. Whether a body can continue, and how members allocate time from their lives, directly determine what the evening can contain. Collective intensity has a specific process of production; final excitement cannot by itself establish a liberation shared by everyone.
He Fa stresses both equal respect and the necessity of continuing. Their coexistence has more intellectual weight than a frictionless account of co-creation: the ability to voice an opinion does not mean equal exposure to pressure. Performance, rehearsal schedule and backstage accounts should be read against one another. His importance here lies partly in organization and documentation. Assigning the entire production to him would conceal the collaborative structure through which it became possible.
The limits of this reading
Participant accounts remain individual accounts; the process is not presented as a verified therapeutic or collective psychological effect.

2012 / Photography, light box
Fragments
Dense horizontal bands divide the image into adjoining fragments.
Fragments, 2012. Portfolio image 1 of 1.
Image record & citation
hf-img-2f18cb7b1ffc
Fragments formed from narrow strips and colour blocks
Extremely narrow horizontal image strips accumulate across the composition in gray, brown, blue and green. Vertical joins separate unequal rectangular regions. Recognisable scenery is compressed into dense linear bands and granular textures rather than a continuous view.
Artist
He Fa
Date
March 2012
Recorded dimensions
2400 × 1250 mm
Recorded medium
Light box
Images and presentation
Fragments is a wide horizontal image filled with narrow bands. Grey, blue, green and earth-toned textures lie alongside one another in separate blocks. The breaks between bands are immediately visible; closer inspection finds textures that resemble fragments of natural scenes. Reading the whole and identifying its details call for different kinds of attention.
The portfolio separates the title from the image: name, dimensions and date appear first, followed by the dense field of texture. The work is recorded as a light box measuring 2400 × 1250 mm, dated March 2012. The full horizontal image is retained here so that differences between blocks and the seams joining them remain visible together.

2021–2023 / Interactive theatre, a voting game and a transcript archive
Saturday Four-Hour Duel Club
Six fighters and a four-hour countdown: votes held by the audience continually change the event.
Public Duel Club poster announcing 23 October 2021; the poster alone does not establish the event’s actual occurrence.
Image record & citation
hf-img-44692e8b1973
Duel Club public poster with a smiling face
A bright-red vertical poster places the large black Duel Club title above a black smiling face with cyan-green eyes and a magenta mouth. Six vertical name columns sit beneath small circular slogan elements, followed by the date 2021/10/23, Chinese calendrical text and logos at both lower corners.
He Fa’s role
Purples co-initiation and collaborative development of its game models
Co-initiators
Purples: Shen Bolun, He Fa and Shao Yifan
Performance
23 October 2021, 24KiCK Fight Academy, Botai branch, Beijing
Transcript publication
10 April 2023, Hours One to Four
Turning the ring into a theatre of judgment
Saturday Four-Hour Duel Club is a performance and game model within Purples. Six recruits entered as “fighters,” bringing their lived experiences while seeking audience support. The event on 23 October 2021 took place in a Beijing boxing gym, with a four-hour countdown and five eliminations. Performance, persuasion and audience votes determined who remained, rather than fighting skills.
The call required no professional performance experience and proposed several workshop-style rehearsals. The ring, countdown, voting marbles and scales made a mechanism of allocation visible: some people competed for attention while others occupied the position of spectator and judge. He Fa co-initiated Purples with Shen Bolun and Shao Yifan, and this work developed within that collaboration.
Writing after the four hours
Four transcripts published in 2023 preserve Hours One to Four, keeping the host’s, fighters’ and spectators’ voices within the unfolding event. The call and record can be read together to examine how a rule was used through speech, questions, silence and voting. Original role labels are retained without assigning unverified real names to their lines.
A later presentation proposal
Voting with marbles in the contemporary event materials and counting votes through drinks in the later Presentation Proposal belong to different versions. The proposal retains six fighters, four hours and five eliminations while setting out another arrangement of rules and scheduling. Read these proposed conditions alongside the record of the event on 23 October 2021.
See source pages 13–14 of the Presentation Proposal. The contemporary call and four-hour transcripts remain linked on this page.

CLOSE READING / 2026 CURATORIAL INTERPRETATION
Saturday Four-Hour Duel Club
What changes when the audience can vote—and what stays?
Work date: 2021–2023
Reading: 2026
Begin with what happens in the work
Six “fighters” enter a boxing venue, seeking audience support through a four-hour countdown and five elimination rounds.
Marbles and weighing scales take part in deciding who stays; victory is not determined by fighting skill.
The ring borrows the space of competition and turns the contest toward securing support. Performance, lived experience, persuasion and audience judgment share a limited duration. This is not a simple advance from passive watching to active participation. Voting has consequences, but elimination restricts those consequences to staying or leaving. Spectators judge while fighters must keep seeking retention. The difference between these positions becomes materially visible in scales and a countdown.
The four-hour transcript published in 2023 adds a record of the rules being used. Readers can move from the invitation’s promises into live speech and examine what hosting, questioning, silence and persuasion did to the arrangement. Any discussion of the work’s politics should stay with these distributions rather than announcing democracy simply because a vote exists. Rules begin an event, and people within it reveal wishes and frustrations the rules have not settled.
The limits of this reading
The performance year is distinguished from transcript publication; lines are not assigned real identities without a verified correspondence.
Sources for this reading

sources.title: How to Eat a Banana?
sources.text:
2021 / P4X workshop
How to Eat a Banana?
A familiar act becomes a question to experience together.
Original cover of the 2021 P4X workshop notice, retaining its source proportions.
Image record & citation
hf-img-88b28f79cdb2
How to Eat a Banana?: coloured-fibre title image
Fine red, green, purple and blue lines spread outward across a black horizontal image, gathering around the centre like fibres or streamlines. Vertical yellow title characters pass through the cluster, with portions cut off at the upper and lower edges.
He Fa’s role
Initiator
Announcement
24 March 2021
Announced schedule
28 March, 18:00–20:00, P4 Theater; no stated participant limit
An everyday action as an opening
How to Eat a Banana? was announced as a P4X workshop, explicitly naming He Fa as its initiator. The notice offers neither a preliminary theory nor an elaborate plot. Instead, it invites people to “experience together” the question during a scheduled two-hour session. Food, bodies, actions and the people nearby provide an immediately approachable starting point.
This archive reads the title as a way of questioning a familiar action. Knowing how to eat a banana does not give a collective event a predetermined answer. The title brings a usually overlooked act into shared attention and leaves the “how” to the encounter. This describes the possibility established by the invitation. The surviving short notice does not provide a full exercise sequence or a report of the results, so it is preserved here as workshop documentation.
The voice of the invitation · 2021
“Let us experience together / how to eat a banana?” The exaggerated declaration and extended exclamation marks that follow make the invitation itself playful. Its modest scale offers a concrete entry into P4’s use of improvisation, limited time and shared participation.

sources.text:
2017 / Documentary video
Fa’s review
A 2017 studio review with a live camera feed in a VR headset: four historical listings and three studio recordings newly published in 2026.
Name in the source
Fa He
Completion date in the list
28 April 2017
Recordings in the historical list
4
Original category
Documentary
Newly published studio records
3 recordings, organised and published in 2026 on P4 Theater Archive
Current project title
Fa re-review; listed contemporaneously as Fa’s review
Four recordings
Fa He Work Sample List, preserved with material from the CCA period, lists four recordings titled Fa’s review: 01 runs 23 minutes 35 seconds; 02, 40 seconds; 03, 17 minutes 12 seconds. A fourth is labelled “dong dong perspective” and runs 1 hour and 33 seconds. All four share the completion date 28 April 2017.
The list also names advancement-review information, a statement prepared for the review and a statement for Fa’s review as important material within the video. This page retains the original English title, viewpoint label, durations and four historical links. The three studio recordings newly published in 2026 form a separate group; the two lists are not treated as item-for-item equivalents or as a complete event timeline.
Newly published studio records
In 2026, He Fa revisited this 2017 project under the title Fa re-review. Three recordings are now public on the P4 Theater Archive channel: IMG_6298 provides a long studio view, MAH01308 records the opening discussion, and MAH01310 records waiting and the final discussion. Each retains its own shot sequence, camera position and location sound. They are gathered in a dedicated project playlist.
The artist confirms that the participant’s VR headset showed the phone camera’s live view of the same studio and review scene. A person in the room could also encounter that room through the device, bringing the review’s own viewing relations into the project. The account of the headset’s image source and mechanism follows the artist’s explanation.
The artist’s statement before the review
An English statement retained for the advancement review repeatedly asks whether the speaker is an artist. Beginning with art education and artistic identity, He Fa connects artificial intelligence’s capacity to learn tools with human choices made when certainty and expression fail. It provides a contemporaneous textual context for the experiments with language, performance and identity in Fa’s review.
The statement’s claims about artificial intelligence belong to the artist’s thinking at the time. Their place in the work is preserved here without presenting them as technically verified predictions.

← Back to the project
Nobody's Return
Thirteen-part performance monologue · Final Chinese text / editorial English translation
He Fa reads the text live while He Yu performs with a candle; at the end, they sit facing each other.
01
中文原稿
回来。

……回

来过。

鞋底还是湿的

最初是两个，一个站在这里，

一个……

一。
一。

这样
算
不算

两个

白天我已经走了

走了以后才看见

门后面是竹子，竹子后面

那个，别叫她。
她正在从一个人经过的地方经过。
水面没有抬头。

你的脸怎么还在这里。
拿走了吗。
我记得拿走了。
ENGLISH TRANSLATION
Come back.

…come

have been back.

The soles are still wet

At first there were two, one standing here,

one…

One.
One.

Does this
count
as

two

By daylight I had already left

Only after leaving did I see

behind the door is bamboo, behind the bamboo

That one, don't call her.
She is passing through a place someone passed through.
The water did not look up.

Why is your face still here.
Was it taken away.
I remember taking it away.
02
中文原稿
半步。

再半步就不是这个地方了。
你先不要跨。

那只手还没有来。

手指到了，剩下的在昨天。
昨天下午……
不，夜里。

我们刚刚决定永远不再见面。
刚刚。
永远有这么近吗。

放在旁边。
先把永远放在旁边。

天台上有一把椅子，坐着的人不是椅子。有时候是。
她喝多了。眼睛没有。
眼睛还要什么。

风。
一点点

。

呼吸吹成哭，哭吹成车，车已经开过去了，

你听见了吗。

不是问你

你坐远一点。
又
太远了。
ENGLISH TRANSLATION
Half a step.

Another half step and it won't be this place anymore.
Don't step across yet.

That hand hasn't arrived.

The fingers are here, the rest is in yesterday.
Yesterday afternoon…
no, at night.

We just decided never to see each other again.
Just now.
Can forever be this close.

Put it to one side.
Put forever to one side for now.

Gewu Studio / Products and Spatial Experiments

Studio
Gewu Studio
He Fa’s role
Co-founder and artistic director
Archive scope
Three product projects and two spatial proposals
A collaborative studio practice
This archive is drawn from Gewu Studio’s half-year report. It brings together five projects: Wave Pen, Tantan, Cornices, a screen for Phoenix Island in Sanya, and lighting for Beijing’s 768 Creative Park. As co-founder and artistic director, He Fa contributed to the studio’s creative direction, conceptual development, form studies and philosophical inquiry. Individual products and commissions are presented here as a collaborative studio archive.
Products: curves, repetition and generation
Wave Pen and Cornices turn continuous curves and layered structures into objects for use and wear. Tantan appears alongside them in the studio’s product series. Product photographs in the report make it possible to read these projects together with the contemporaneous Twelve Water Lamps.
Space: screens and light
The report also includes a screen designed for a Type A residence at Phoenix Island in Sanya and lighting for a venue in Beijing’s 768 Creative Park. The surviving images are design renderings. They record how curves and light were intended to enter architectural space; they do not establish completion of construction.
Credits and documentation
These products and spatial proposals are presented as records of the studio’s collaborative practice. He Fa’s work encompassed photography, conceptual development, form exploration and artistic direction. The making of the objects and authorship of their images are recorded separately.
Qingfeng Fuping: a view that changes with the body
The Qingfeng Fuping proposal designs a seascape screen for the entrance of a Type A show residence in the Phoenix Island business clubhouse, Sanya. It treats the entrance as a point where an interior view reaches the sea, connecting screen, home and seascape through looking. The proposal records an overall width of 2 m and height of 6 m, combining 55 distinct horizontal curved elements with a concealed straight framework.
The document also preserves form studies, three views of a single frame layer and a proposal for mortise-and-tenon assembly. As viewers change position, overlapping curves form different relationships. The document’s idea of “flow” refers both to the image of water and to the movement of a person.
Source documents: 清风拂屏, pp. 3, 6, 11, 14, 15, 16, 17, 20.
Ten names for Tantan
The studio’s Tantan naming draft develops ten homophonous or near-homophonous Chinese names: 弹弹, 忐忐, 探探, 叹叹, 昙昙, 坦坦, 檀檀, 潭潭, 谈谈 and 袒袒. Each links a disposition to a flower: 忐忐 connects shyness with begonia, while 潭潭 connects mystery with winter cherry blossom. The formal series thus also has a linguistic system built from sound, written meaning and botanical associations.
The draft documents the series’ naming concept and expressive method; it does not by itself establish production or exhibition details for all ten groups.
Source documents: 格物Tantan文案.
Jinhua Award medal and trophy proposal
The studio’s initial Jinhua Award proposal brings together a ploughshare, earth, sun and a V for victory. A transformed V frames the medal; the trophy develops that outline into curves and volumes seen from different directions. The nine-page document preserves two variants, four elevation renderings and a sequence of spatial studies through 360 degrees.
The document is credited to GEWU Studio, and the medal rendering is inscribed “2013.” This date belongs to the award inscription in the image; the initial draft provides no record of selection or completed production.
Source documents: 金铧奖——方案初稿, pp. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.

The Forbidden City
An architectural outline remains recognizable as details disperse through overlapping images.
The Forbidden City, 2009–2012. Portfolio image 1 of 1.
Image record & citation

故宫｜屋顶与人群片段
Overlapping roof tiers and fragments of a crowd occupy the pale centre. Their edges fade towards a white outer margin.
《故宫》系列，作品记录为2009–2012；题名依据档案关联，不推定具体游览或拍摄日期。

Artist

Recorded medium

Images and presentation
The Forbidden City appears in the portfolio as a single square image. A roof and the outline of a building occupy the centre, while colour, vertical lines and figure-like traces disperse around them. Instead of a sharply bounded architectural view, slightly displaced images remain visible together. Their overlaps darken; their edges become diffuse.
From a distance, the building coalesces into a broad form. Closer attention finds lines and areas of colour that cannot easily be assigned to one stable instant. The effect of superimposition is visible, but the source does not specify the number of exposures, the compositing procedure or an exact camera position. It records an archival pigment print, 520 × 520 mm, dated March 2009–March 2012.

sources.title: Hallucination
sources.text:
2020 / Proscenium theatre and production practice
Hallucination
A theatre production connecting Shixiang with the emergence of the 3P group.
Original cover of the 2020 announcement, retaining its source proportions.
Image record & citation
hf-img-59a6844d7f83
Hallucination: oversized title and event details
An oversized black Chinese character “致” dominates a white horizontal crop over a pale pink circle and fine red line. Vertical text on the right gives an August 15 performance time and “p4剧场” as the venue.
He Fa’s role
Production collaborator, according to his 2022 retrospective
Production collaborators
He Fa and Zhang Shaohua; Huang Lucang subsequently joined the production
Announced performance
15 August 2020, P4 Theater
The work and its production context
A P4 notice dated 8 August 2020 invited audiences to Hallucination on 15 August. The brief notice preserves the title, announced performance and original visual. He Fa’s 2022 retrospective situates the work within a longer sequence: after returning to China, he resumed Shixiang with Zhang Shaohua, then worked on Hallucination; Huang Lucang joined the production, and the 3P group formed in this period.
Within this personal archive, Hallucination documents He Fa’s involvement in bringing a production into being. A proscenium play provided a defined production format, while rehearsal, collaboration and documentation extended the work beyond the stage. Reading the documents together helps explain the later intertwining of watching, performing and recording within P4. This account of continuity is an editorial reading across the dated sources.
He Fa’s retrospective · 2022
“We then resumed work on the proscenium play Hallucination. At this point Huang Lucang also joined the production, and the 3P group was formed.” This retrospective is the direct basis for identifying He Fa’s production involvement and collaborators.
From Shixiang research to an open call
In A Future That Seems to Be but Is Not, dated April 27, 2021, He Fa recalls that he and Zhang Shaohua had been developing Shixiang before seeking wider participation through Hallucination. He describes an online call, numerous applications, several interview rounds, cast selection, intensive rehearsal, and set and lighting work. His account explicitly says the production was successfully staged, adding an organizer’s retrospective confirmation to the earlier recruitment material.
The same essay places Hallucination, Cocoon and The Rooftop Howler in a sequence of projects assembled through open calls. Calling himself one of the venue’s organizers, He Fa also acknowledges that his judgments could affect scripts and collective decisions. The account documents production conditions and the organizer’s position; it does not supply a director’s credit, complete plot or final performance version.

sources.title: Hamlet’s Mirror / Four-screen CAFAM Proposal
sources.text:
2016 / Proposal for four-screen projection, live performance and real-time video
Hamlet’s Mirror / Four-screen CAFAM Proposal
From one screen to a four-sided enclosure, extending the displacement between audiences, performers and images.
Four-screen proposal for Hamlet’s Mirror, 2016. Original rendering from the CAFAM proposal signed by He Fa and Zhang Aoshuang, p. 5.
Image record & citation
hf-img-40cc2f151d6e
Four-screen proposal rendering for Hamlet’s Mirror
A proposal rendering uses four black screens to enclose an open square, each displaying different figures and performance imagery. Magenta outer bands label spectator areas and green inner strips identify performance zones, while the oblique view distinguishes screen orientation, central emptiness and surrounding positions against grey-white ground.
Co-creators
He Fa and Zhang Aoshuang / FakingAosome
CAFAM proposal: signed date
5 September 2016
Original version
June–December 2015, P4 Theater, Beijing
Status
Four-screen expansion proposal; final realization not verified
A collaboration by FakingAosome
The proposal dated 5 September 2016 is signed by He Fa and Zhang Aoshuang. Its team introduction states that they founded FakingAosome in 2015 to explore theatre, the internet and visual language. Hamlet’s Mirror is identified as the group’s first project, developed at P4 Theater in Beijing between June and December 2015.
From one screen to four
The document describes the 2015 first version as using one screen, one performer, one projector and one video camera. The new proposal encloses a space with four screens, marking audience and performance areas in pink and green. It retains an eight-act structure to be realized through live action and real-time projection.
Screens as spatial relationships
The authors treat the body’s interruption of projection as a change of stage and an image projected onto a body as another space. The four-screen proposal transfers displacement within an image to relationships between screens, nesting the person, the image and the viewing position within one another.
Proposal status
The document is explicitly presented as a proposal for the Third CAFAM Biennale and includes a spatial rendering, implementation requirements and an equipment budget. It establishes a proposed expansion in 2016, without by itself proving realization at the biennale.
A separately dated Theory Theatre proposal
A separately retained four-page “Theory Theatre” proposal is signed by Zhang Aoshuang and He Fa on its final page and dated 10 August 2016. Page 3 proposes an enclosure of four screens, with audience and performance areas marked in pink and green respectively. It is a separate document from the CAFAM proposal bearing the signed date 5 September 2016. The documents should be cited separately: 10 August is not the signed date recorded in the latter, nor does this evidence establish the CAFAM proposal’s actual submission date or the exhibition’s realization.
Archival document review · 30 September 2026. Source: the four-page “Theory Theatre” proposal, pp. 3–4, signed and dated 10 August 2016. English is an editorial translation; “Theory Theatre” translates 理论剧院.
From a four-page to a five-page proposal
A page-by-page comparison shows that the five-page CAFAM proposal signed and dated 5 September 2016 adds an introduction to FakingAosome and descriptions of four projects to the four-page “Theory Theatre” proposal dated 10 August. It retains the spatial diagram of an enclosure formed by four screens. The added introduction places Hamlet’s Mirror in the context of the team’s other work. Both documents are signed by He Fa and Zhang Aoshuang; the textual revisions and the reuse of the diagram are not evidence that two exhibitions were realized.
Archival document comparison · 30 September 2026. Sources: the four-page “Theory Theatre” proposal dated 10 August 2016 and the five-page proposal for the Third CAFAM Biennale dated 5 September 2016. These are the dates recorded with the signatures. English is an editorial translation.

sources.text:
2023 / Collective puppet-making, role play and an evolving theatrical environment
Happiness Kingdom
Citizens emerge from discarded materials, and the characters made by participants continue to act and live.
Puppets and a setting for Happiness Kingdom, published in April 2023.
Image record & citation
hf-img-96fc2c6aca78
Oblique view of a yellow face within its setting
An oblique view approaches a yellow round face with blue-white eyes, a red smile and green forehead decoration amid outward red-purple strips. A large linear flower appears on the deep-blue panel behind, with additional objects at right separating the face, supports and background into different depths.
He Fa’s role
Co-design of formats, rules and models, and organisation through P4
Credits in the collaborative archive
Happiness Kingdom, Shi Jiating, Tian Xinyi, Bangbang and participants
Documented strands
Dream Factory; Seven Princes and the Strawberry Princess; image-making activities
He Fa’s account
His signed May 2024 text lists it among formats he designed or helped design
Entering a role through making
Happiness Kingdom first invited participants to make puppets together from discarded objects, paper and lightweight clay. Makers gave each character colours, a personality, allergens and skills, establishing its identity as a citizen of the fictional world. Images published in late April 2023 already show colourful figures, handmade settings and installations. The Dream Factory call for 1–7 May invited further participants to make props for subsequent theatrical activity.
The May call for Seven Princes and the Strawberry Princess turned audience members into visiting characters. They were asked to bring a small handmade gift and enter through conversation, talents and improvised games. Public texts by Shi Jiating, Tian Xinyi, Bangbang and others extended the world from different roles. June’s face-painting and July’s Trial of Shijiating expanded character-making through bodies, colour and collective construction.
The scope of co-design
In his signed 2024 retrospective, He Fa includes Happiness Kingdom among the rule-based formats he “designed or helped design.” This supports a co-design credit while characters and texts retain their respective authors. The archive presents the realised puppets and settings alongside the announced event structures. A proposal to film and edit an event remains a proposal, rather than a completed film credit.

CLOSE READING / 2026 CURATORIAL INTERPRETATION
Happiness Kingdom
Does making a character change how one can enter a story?
Work date: 2023
Reading: 2026
Begin with what happens in the work
Participants make figures from discarded materials, paper and lightweight clay, assigning colours, personalities, skills and other features.
Later invitations ask visitors to bring handmade gifts and enter roles through conversation, performances and improvisational games.
A world begins with a small object made by hand. A figure’s personality is not prewritten in a hidden database; paper and clay can change the character its maker imagines. Gifts, conversation and games then carry those identities into exchanges among people. Making objects and making theatre are not separate categories here. A thing is made, acquires a name and relations, and becomes something another person can answer when entering the story.
There is an echo, with differences, of Gewu’s lamps. The lamps fix generative rules into an object; Happiness Kingdom lets objects receive further names and uses from other people. Yet the fictional world still has invitations, points of entry and dates. Openness does not mean an absence of structure. The portfolio should give each maker and initiator a clear position, allowing visitors to enter through He Fa’s work and continue toward others’ works rather than absorbing every contribution into a collective label.
The limits of this reading
Plans to make a film are not counted as a completed film. Other people’s characters and texts do not become He Fa’s individual works.

Based on the 2023 figure-making and activity texts. He Fa’s signed 2024 recollection supports his co-design role.

2011 / Photography, light box
Illusion
Six bodily gestures appear suspended against a white field.
Illusion, 2011. Portfolio image 1 of 6.
Image record & citation
hf-img-a502b5f05a6b
Illusion: sideways leap and lifted hair
A nude figure is suspended sideways against a white vertical field, with both legs bent backward and arms held near the chest. Hair flares upward and rightward. Extensive empty space isolates the body from any visible setting.
Artist
He Fa
Date
September–October 2011
Recorded dimensions
400 × 520 mm
Recorded medium
Light box
Images and presentation
The portfolio presents Illusion as six vertical photographs, arranged in pairs across three pages. A continuous white background leaves no visible ground, support or clear spatial boundary. Hair, arms and bent legs indicate different directions of movement; changes in posture distinguish one photograph from the next.
Placed beside one another, the photographs allow one arrested gesture to be compared with another. They offer moments of movement, but the portfolio does not number them as successive steps. The title page dates the light-box work to September–October 2011 and records dimensions of 400 × 520 mm. All six photographs are presented here as separate images.

Iceberg
A small office and fifteen spectators: spatial proximity becomes part of the work.
Iceberg documentation, P4 Theater.
Image record & citation
hf-img-16b4de3b28ee
Iceberg | Project documentation
People sit along opposite sides of a dim room, leaving a tiled passage through the centre. Purple light frames the rear window and red light washes the walls, while a white circular pool of light and human shadows occupy the lower-right foreground.
People seated opposite one another under purple-red lighting. The work record gives 2021–2022; the specific event and capture date are unverified.

Production.
HE FA’S ROLE
Producer
Year
2021–2022
Medium
Live theatre, spatial installation and collective creation
Role
Producer
Further reading
North Wind Theatre: Iceberg preview
↗
Post-performance editorial on Iceberg
↗
Eight makers and fifteen spectators entered the same small office; Iceberg was performed at 19:30 on 1 January 2022.
03
Project statement
Iceberg was developed by eight makers and opened to an audience of fifteen inside a small office. Crowding, obstruction, silence and the difficulty of entering or leaving directly changed how the event could be seen.
The performance took place at 19:30 on 1 January 2022. Makers and spectators shared the same room without the stable distance of a proscenium stage.
A line through the work
When spectators cannot retreat to a distance, what kind of bodily relation does looking become?
Two venue disruptions before Iceberg took shape
On December 7, 2021, He Fa described meeting Qu Wenhao, planning a production and forming a group again. After the Diaosutai venue stopped opening in June, a proposed ninth production initiated by Qu was halted. They began recruiting in a Wangjing office to develop Qu’s Iceberg. He Fa delegated most organizing work to Qu while occupied elsewhere; another venue problem arose in September. Iceberg’s development thus involved repeated changes of space, people and organization.
When restarting, the two decided to discuss shared values before forming North Wind Theatre. The article explicitly credits Qu with writing the nine-point declaration; He Fa endorsed it and joined the invitation. Its principles include respecting an initiator’s impulse, bringing personal concerns into roles, expressing views openly and addressing disagreement. The record therefore retains Qu’s authorship of the declaration and their joint initiation of the company.

CLOSE READING / 2026 CURATORIAL INTERPRETATION
Iceberg
What does viewing become when there is no distant position?
Work date: 2021–2022
Reading: 2026
Begin with what happens in the work
Eight makers and fifteen spectators occupy an office of a little over ten square metres.
The public archive retains live material, smoke tests and post-performance discussion and criticism.
The space gives no one a frontal position from which everything can be safely surveyed. Another body blocks the view, and one’s own movement changes a neighbour’s sightline. Silence, crowding and difficulty moving become concrete materials. The intensity cannot be reproduced simply by enlarging a video. It comes from the bodily cost of looking in limited space and from the impossibility of imagining the spectator as an eye that leaves the event untouched.
Yet physical closeness proves neither a deep relation nor equal willingness to participate. Spatial facts should coexist with differing audience accounts rather than translating every discomfort into proof of artistic success. He Fa’s production role deserves a concrete description of how venue, schedule, light and documentation enabled collective work. The site can begin with the identifiable office and viewing positions, then let footage and criticism open that small space further.
The limits of this reading
Still photographs and plans do not reproduce the live experience. The producer credit is not rewritten as sole director.
Sources for this reading
Based on performance records, the public work page and its linked North Wind Theatre archive.

2009 / Photography, light box
Gathering
Tables, rooms and snow-covered ground form circular arrangements of distinct everyday scenes.
Gathering, 2009. Portfolio image 1 of 4.
Image record & citation
hf-img-f3fc70e2be6d
Gathering: circular montage around a dining table
Dishes, bowls, chopsticks and drinks spread across a dining table assembled into a circle. Seated people radiate around its outer edge. Straight photographic boundaries and overlaps remain visible under warm indoor light against a brown surrounding ground.
Artist
He Fa
Date
September 2009
Recorded dimensions
512 × 512 mm
Recorded medium
Light box
Images and presentation
The four images in Gathering share circular or sphere-like arrangements but contain different scenes. One gathers food, people and a room around a dining table. Another retains the purple light of an interior. The remaining images turn to a snowy courtyard and a room containing a person. Displaced edges, cuts and repetitions remain visible throughout.
No single central object organizes all of these scenes. Tables, walls, floors and people acquire different orientations through the assembled photographs. The images retain recognizable things while rearranging their usual spatial relationships. The portfolio dates the light-box work to September 2009, records dimensions of 512 × 512 mm, and places all four images under the title Gathering.

sources.text:
2021 / Theatre event, 3P creative observation and exhibition proposal
Kill the Rose: 3P—Watching, Performing, Recording
Cameras and writers enter rehearsal, making documentation a form of participation that can affect the event.
Image from the 2021 production-team and 3P group introduction.
Image record & citation
hf-img-c6860c5a83ef
杀死那朵玫瑰花｜工作桌旁的团队
An overhead photograph shows people sitting or standing around a yellow table crowded with laptops, cups, food containers and small objects. Some look upward toward the camera. Glass and long branches line the right, beneath overlaid “KILL THE ROSE X P4” text.
《杀死那朵玫瑰花：3P 看、演、拍》团队介绍所刊合照：俯视画面中，多名人物围在摆有电脑、纸张、杯子和器材的工作桌旁；左侧保留KILL THE ROSE X P4字样。来源文献发表于2021-05-24；拍摄日和具体场次未核实。
Copyright: P4 Theater
现存记录未单列逐图创作分工；本轮不补写
He Fa’s role
3P group creator; author of the 3P recruitment text
Principal production credits
Initiator/director Liu Ziluo; producer Zheng Anqi; dramaturg Sun Xiaoxing; writer Liu Ke
Published 3P roster
Sun Xiaoxing, He Fa, Li Wenqi, Pian Ziwei and Zhang Haolin
A parallel creative process
The eighth P4U project, Kill the Rose, was introduced as a “wild interactive musical”, with a story involving a leaked photograph and online violence. Alongside the production, He Fa authored a call for 3P creators to enter rehearsals, conversations, interviews and documentation. The public introduction of 24 May lists him in the 3P group and separately credits the production’s director, writer and team.
The 3P call welcomed photography, writing, sound, moving image and other media. It required at least three releases during the monthly cycle and proposed an exhibition in the non-stage areas opening on the day of the performance. Observers were considered part of the environment, capable of affecting the event. Documentation therefore had its own rhythm and public form, speaking while rehearsal was still underway and bringing participants’ judgements into the work.
He Fa’s source text · 2021
“A sincere observer continually includes themselves within the system.” Watching, performing and recording become a way of working together. The exhibition and release frequency were proposed rules; this page distinguishes that rule text from the published roster of creators.

CLOSE READING / 2026 CURATORIAL INTERPRETATION
Kill the Rose: 3P—Watching, Performing, Recording
What happens to an event when its record is published before it ends?
Work date: 2021
Reading: 2026
Begin with what happens in the work
The 3P open call allowed multiple media and required at least three publications within a month.
The rules proposed an exhibition outside the stage area opening with the performance; stage-production and 3P credits are listed separately.
3P does not wait until the play is finished to certify that it happened. Observers enter rehearsal, interviews and conversations and publish during the same production cycle. A remark can already have been read, judged and brought back into the room before opening night. Documentation is not merely the event’s later shadow: it becomes a condition of its continuation. Photography, writing and performance cross one another through an actual rhythm of publication.
Acknowledging the observer’s presence does not erase differences between observer and observed. Editing power, publication timing and the consequences of circulation still require particular decisions. The original rules leave ownership for members to negotiate, showing that even the identity of a work’s author is produced through collaboration. A presentation should unfold stage production and documentation in parallel, with their separate makers and dates, so viewers can see one event generating different works that affect one another.
The limits of this reading
Three publications and a simultaneous exhibition opening were requirements; each member’s actual output needs its own publication evidence.
Sources for this reading
Based on He Fa’s signed 3P open call of 13 May 2021 and the production / 3P roster of 24 May.

sources.text:
2010 / Photography, archival pigment prints
Large Portraits / Portraits
Four portraits unfold alongside three enlarged details of each.
Portrait — He Fa, 2010. Full portrait; 2310 × 2430 mm, archival pigment print.
Image record & citation
hf-img-2aaefbab4b70
Portrait — He Fa: complete frontal view
He Fa faces the camera in a close portrait with thin-framed glasses, tousled short hair and closed lips. A blurred background shifts from dark green on the left to pale gray on the right, without grid lines across the face.
Artist
He Fa
Date
2010
Portrait — He Fa
2310 × 2430 mm
Portrait — Yang Chen
1350 × 1500 mm
Portrait — Huazai
1240 × 1430 mm
Portrait — Bowen
930 × 1020 mm
From the portrait to its details
The 17-page portfolio unfolds in four groups: He Fa, Yang Chen, Huazai and Bowen. Each begins with a full portrait followed by three pages of enlarged details—forehead, hair, eye, nose, lips, ear or hand. The sitters retain their own postures, clothing and lighting; they are not standardized into an identity-photograph format.
The sequence moves from a person to details, then returns to another person. A full portrait allows a face to be apprehended as a whole, while detail pages attend to skin, hair, reflected light and incidental gestures. Each portrait has its own recorded physical dimensions; all are identified as archival pigment prints from 2010. Names follow the captions in the portfolio.
Another record of the same portrait
Portrait — He Fa in the 2010 portfolio and I in the 2012 record use the same portrait. The earlier image is vertical and has no grid; the later image is square and gridded. The portfolios give different titles, dates and dimensions. This site retains both documentary versions and connects them through related works.
Works & details
Portrait — He Fa, 2010. detail 1; 2310 × 2430 mm, archival pigment print.
Image record & citation

2017 / Collective art project proposal
Long Long Ago / Project Proposal
A proposal for meeting across neighbourhoods and taking turns to host events.
Collective named in the text
Long Long Ago Group
Status
Proposal; no realized programme established by the records reviewed here
Proposed location
Districts of San Francisco
Proposed event period
1 January 2018–31 January 2019
Working together in the proposal
The proposal identifies shared experience, life, time and space as its starting points. It envisages selecting artists from different districts of San Francisco to form a new collective, then travelling between their districts to hold events. Each participating artist would host and curate the event in their own area. Performance, installation, exhibition and other forms were encouraged, in homes or public spaces.
The text sets out recruitment, announcements and a year-long sequence of events, through which different communities might encounter one another repeatedly. These are plans within a proposal, not evidence of a realized exhibition or public programme. The ideas and timetable are retained as a document of possible collective work. The body names the group; He Fa’s specific responsibilities require further documentation.
Archive note
Based on Fa He_AltEx_LongLongAgo.docx. The dates 2017–2019 refer to the application milestones and planned events in the proposal, not a verified production or realization period. The proposed 27 districts, 54-week schedule and participant numbers are not reported as completed outcomes. The original English project name is retained.

sources.text:
2020 / Screenings, collective discussion and an ongoing participatory practice
P4 Screenings: Reflections Between Us
Moving from watching films to sharing personal accounts, the project calls its discussions “self-screening.”
Original cover for P4 Screenings, November 2020.
Image record & citation
hf-img-ebe94ca656c6
P4 Screenings cover with yellow lettering
A narrow black cover centres large glowing yellow p4放映 lettering with slender strokes nearly filling the image height. Rows of dark Chinese phrases repeat behind with subtle red-blue variations, creating two contrasting layers of bright title and low-contrast text texture without figures or photographic imagery.
He Fa’s role
Co-organisation, programme rules and authored project descriptions
First cycle
Ended 16 August 2020; September account records 15 screenings
Programme revision
November 2020; the signed article reports nearly 40 sessions
Location
P4 Theater, Diaosutai, Beijing
From screening to self-screening
At the beginning of 2020, He Fa and his P4 collaborators began watching recordings of theatre within the venue, then gradually opened the sessions to others. His September account records fifteen screenings and discussions in a first cycle ending on 16 August, and says he attended every one. A film supplied the starting point; afterwards, participants sat under the stage lights to share impressions, associations and personal experiences. Their accounts became a second “screening,” shifting the gathering towards listening to one another.
The second cycle connected the film, a break and discussion, with fewer than fifteen participants per session. Selections rotated through death, sexuality, self-portraiture and history, and participants could propose their own videos. The September rules explicitly left discussions unrecorded to preserve privacy, establishing a different relation to documentation from P4’s camera-centred projects.
Reorganising the programme into five parts
In November, He Fa reorganised the experience of nearly forty sessions into paper, screen, self, glass and dream screenings, proposing a programme from Sunday afternoon to Monday morning. Paper Screening developed as a distinct practice that moved from drawing into conversation. This page records the programme’s two stages; the extended timetable remains the published proposal rather than a claim that every component ran every week.

sources.text:
2015–present / Long-term art practice, live work and archives
P4 Theater
Spaces, participants, events and documentation change one another through sustained work.
P4 Theater documentation. The project connects performances, shared work and the public archive.
Image record & citation
hf-img-eb07f0aa00e9
Standing figure before a seated floor group
Several people sit cross-legged along a grey-black wall, facing a dark-clothed figure standing with their back to the camera at front right. Overhead light catches the central floor and pale clothing, while cropped bodies and deep shadows frame the seated gathering.
HE FA’S ROLE
Co-initiated with Zhang Shaohua; long-term host and organizer
Year
2015–present
Medium
Long-term artistic platform, performance, workshops, moving image and writing
Role
Co-initiator / long-term artistic lead and organiser
External link
↗
Further reading
The Evolution of P4 Theater
↗
Shadow Counterpoint, GIF edition
↗
The idea of P4 began in 2015 and its first public work appeared in 2016. He Fa has since sustained its projects, spaces, moving images and writing.
02
Project statement
Around 2015, He Fa and Zhang Shaohua initiated P4 Theater in Beijing. Zhang Aoshuang took part in its early conception and co-curated the first public performance, Shadow Counterpoint, with He Fa in 2016. He Fa has continued as P4’s long-term artistic lead and organiser.
P4 projects have entered former factories, a small office, a boxing space, bookstores and private rooms. Site, participant identity, audience routes and filming conditions are not backdrops; they directly alter how the work takes place.
A line through the work
If theatre is first a way of arranging relations, where does a work begin and where can it end?
Enabling participants to initiate work
In his 2024 retrospective, He Fa describes 510 as an incubator operating from a living-room-sized space, where participants rehearsed and went on to form their own groups. The 2025 ten-year archive explicitly distinguishes projects initiated by participants. Together, these documents show how space, calls, publication and mutual support gave new work a starting point. This website preserves that shared relation while keeping the original creative credits.
Meat Grinder · Kousi Theatre
The August 2022 call for Meat Grinder is credited to Zhao Xuan, followed by Kousi Theatre’s declaration and an announcement for a party-format performance on 1 November. Subsequent texts retain voices including Zhao Xuan and Miaoji. He Fa includes the project in P4’s lineage of participant-led work; this chapter documents that platform relationship without adding a directing credit for him.
Kill Mother · Guo Qian
Guo Qian’s call sets out Kill Mother as a three-hour theatre salon for eight participants on 4 June 2023. Each was invited to bring a chosen text to explore relationships with mothers within a theatrical situation. The archive retains this specific public proposal; a separate 2026 after-show text sharing the title is not treated as proof that this 2023 session took place.
The Old Sun Rises on a New Day · Jiarui
Jiarui announced The Old Sun Rises on a New Day on 12 June 2023 as a half-hour theatre salon planned for 17 June, with a poster credit to Wang Yiwen. The original title uses “rises.” Alongside the preceding projects, it remains part of P4’s participant-led archive, linked to its own announcement and retaining its creators rather than substituting the platform’s organisers.
Present, photosynthesis, psychology, permanent
An early visual draft places four words beginning with P beside the P4 theater mark: present, photosynthesis, psychology and permanent. The P4 Preface layout pairs a photograph of the theatre with a text about mutually watching and performing: stepping beyond definitions imposed by others and holding a present moment in an image. These drafts preserve an early articulation of P4’s connection between photography, live presence and participants’ own experience.
Source documents: P4 theater视觉稿（p4-2.pdf）; P4前言.
2019–2021: shared photographic research and a public venue
A Future That Seems to Be but Is Not places P4’s beginnings in He Fa and Zhang Shaohua’s shared photographic work. Former photography classmates, they explored portraiture, performance and emotion, established a venue in Tiantongyuan in 2015, and continued after He Fa returned to China in 2019. He calls the space their laboratory and treats theatre as recruitment, rehearsal, disagreement and public performance together. The 2023 essay Salon of the Rejected and Alliance of Failures describes the 2019 shift as opening the black box to people with few opportunities to use a stage.
Questioning the organizers within the interview
In the first Cocoon interview, He Fa is one of several respondents. He recalls telling participants that different roles did not remove their right to disagree, and hopes relationships might continue beyond the completion of a performance task. A Rooftop Howler interview preserves a counterpoint: as He Fa asks what a performer observed, Zhang Shaohua questions whether the interview imposes a prior assumption, while Huang Lucang notes its movement toward analysis. Together, the voices show organizing methods being discussed and challenged within the process itself.
The public opening in a retained report
An opening-report manuscript retained by the artist records P4’s public opening in Beijing’s Diaosutai art district on 4 June 2016, together with the premiere of Shadow Counterpoint. This dates a specific event and is recorded separately from accounts of preparations in 2015. The manuscript describes Zhang Shaohua and He Fa as founders and Zhang Aoshuang as a co-founder, and records shared work on the theatre’s design, construction and technical systems. These terms follow the manuscript.
Archival document supplement. Source: the retained manuscript “P4 Theater Opening — An Open Theatre as a Cross-disciplinary Laboratory” (title translated). Its original publication has not been verified; passages shared with the project press manuscript are not treated as independent corroboration. English is an editorial translation.

CLOSE READING / 2026 CURATORIAL INTERPRETATION
P4 Theater
How can a container support works while letting them change it?
Work date: 2015–present
Reading: 2026
Begin with what happens in the work
He Fa and Zhang Shaohua developed the early initiative, with Zhang Aoshuang proposing a theatre layout; a black stage adjoined white working and audience areas.
Later work entered offices, a boxing venue, bookshops and other spaces, developing particular forms of recruitment, rehearsal, screening and documentation.
Calling P4 a venue misses much of its work; calling it one enormous individual artwork by He Fa claims too much. It includes renting and adapting spaces, setting project cycles, recruiting strangers, forming collaborations and making works visible. Each task creates conditions and distributes limits. How audiences enter, whether a newcomer can initiate a project, and when rehearsal must end all affect the art that appears.
Its depth should emerge from specific arrangements and encounters rather than a method presumed correct in advance. The early pursuit of photographic truth, time-limited co-creation, participant-led projects and cinema’s later arrangement of the process do not fully coincide. A mature presentation lets these changes illuminate one another and lets individual authors remain findable beyond P4’s shared name. A container’s value lies not only in how much it holds, but in what it enables to develop its own direction.
The limits of this reading
P4 production, He Fa’s organization and his individual authorship are distinct. Different venues do not create an identical spatial experience.

Workshop structure
Material selection, drawing, looking and sharing accounts
Bringing paper onto the stage
Paper Screening grew out of the P4 Screenings programme. The November 2020 description credits the format to collaboration between Lisa (Xue Lixia) and P4, with Lisa initiating and facilitating the sessions. Participants selected brushes, paint and paper, drew under the stage lights, then spoke with others while facing their images. He Fa’s role lies in the broader programme’s organisation and framework; facilitation and the authorship of participants’ drawings retain their separate credits.
The drawing was not the session’s only outcome. Holding an image up for others, describing its associations and listening to responses also formed part of the event. Public photographs document material selection, drawing together and speaking while holding completed work; the report of 26 November also preserves participant reflections. These records establish an enacted collective practice beyond the initial call.
Source terminology and the archive’s approach
The original articles introduced the programme through the terms “art therapy” and “healing through drawing.” This page retains that historical context while describing its materials, space, facilitator and conversational structure, without deriving medical outcomes from testimonials. A December presentation placed images beside poetic responses, continuing the movement between paper, bodies and language.

2023 / Interview archives, collective creation and public documentation
Personal Chronicle / PHA
Begin with a personal account, propose a project publicly, and continue the archive through action.
Original Personal Chronicle concept graphic, 2023.
Image record & citation
hf-img-5ab940cf8b7f
Personal Chronicle PHA: six coloured panels
A red-outlined header reading “个人志 PHA” tops a vertical graphic. Six coloured panels form two columns below, using yellow, green, orange, cyan, red and blue. White Chinese labels and accompanying English words identify the individual sections.
He Fa’s role
Author of the framework and declaration; P4 project organisation
Framework publication
22 March 2023
Six starting points
Programma, Program, Hero, History, Ambition, Ambiance
How the project is structured
In Theatre and Fear, He Fa presents Personal Chronicle / PHA as a way to reorganise P4’s earlier photography, theatre, workshops and actions into a framework for continuing creation. It begins with a two-to-five-hour individual interview in which a narrator recounts their history and ambitions. The recording is retained, with a shorter edit proposed for circulation. After the archive is established, the protagonist can announce a project publicly and invite others to join.
The six starting points impose no fixed medium and may lead to rehearsal, screenings, writing, exhibitions or other actions. The rules propose one project at a time for each protagonist, a public presentation to mark its end, and filming and publication throughout. The transcripts of Zhang Lei and Yun Jianhui published in March 2023 place specific personal accounts beside the framework. This page preserves access to those records while retaining the narrators’ own authorship of their experiences.
He Fa’s source text · 2023
“The act of filming must be embedded in the event’s coming into being.” In Personal Chronicle, interviews, calls for participation, practice and review are connected. The start and end of recording are also used to distinguish collective creation from daily life.
Recording before the project: Yun Jianhui’s self-account
A jointly signed article of February 25, 2023 describes a specific recording session: in early February, He Fa set up a camera and recorded Yun Jianhui speaking for nearly four hours, then made an approximately half-hour edit for circulation. The article also introduces Yun’s documentary Refinding the Compass and announces a March 4 private screening with its director. The documentary belongs to Yun’s practice; He Fa’s recorded and edited material is Yun’s personal-history account.
Yu Yu Yumu: from a personal chronicle to collective writing
The April 6 article calls Yu Yu Yumu the first person to initiate a project after the PHA call. He Fa’s introduction describes two recording sessions and links to a two-hour Personal Chronicle: Full Record. It then changes voice to Yumu’s own proposal for The Thirty-Three: eight collaborators would write fictional lives spanning more than two millennia. The recordings are documented past events; the proposed people and scale of collective writing remained the terms of an open call.

CLOSE READING / 2026 CURATORIAL INTERPRETATION
Personal Chronicle / PHA
How can recording a person enable them to initiate something?
Work date: 2023
Reading: 2026
Begin with what happens in the work
The framework starts with a two-to-five-hour individual interview; after creating a record, the protagonist can initiate a public project.
Programma, Program, Hero, History, Ambition and Ambiance provide six entries; public reporting marks a project’s end.
Personal Chronicle removes life-writing from the résumé’s retrospective format. A narrated past and a desired future share an interview. The record need not merely certify a finished history; it can supply material for a new invitation. Someone listened to by a camera can then become someone inviting others to act. The important shift is this exchange of positions, not an assumption that a long interview is inherently truer than a short video.
The long account, its short edit and a later project should retain their differences. A version edited for circulation shifts emphasis; a public report temporarily concludes an action without concluding the person. If this portfolio borrows the method to present He Fa, it must give history, ambition, completed work and unrealized proposals distinct temporal positions. It can help readers enter someone’s world without allowing the latest arrangement to replace the whole of that person’s life.
The limits of this reading
Narrators’ own films, writing and practices are not reassigned to He Fa. Unproofread transcripts should retain their status labels.

Purples / Purple Action
Roles, rules, speech and collective judgment become theatre within a jointly constructed fictional world.
Closing frame of the Purples project trailer, 2021. Original frame preserved.
HE FA’S ROLE
Co-initiated with Shen Bolun and Shao Yifan
Year
2021

Participatory theatre, role-playing and experiments in organisation
Role
Co-initiated with Shen Bolun and Shao Yifan
Further reading
Duel Club open call
↗
Draw Your Most Beautiful Line of Flight
↗
Purples, also known as Purple Action, is a participatory art project co-initiated by Shen Bolun, He Fa and Shao Yifan. Its project introduction traces a precursor to Shen Bolun’s Coliseum in 2019 and describes its collaborative redevelopment in 2021. Participants enter a fictional world and generate the event through roles, deliberation and organisational action.
05
One project, several theatre models
Purples develops different rules and live situations within a shared fictional world. The Project Introduction presents Final Solution as an organisation within that world and names its deliberative mechanism the “Final Solution assembly model.” Coliseum is a related development strand whose scope depends on the particular document version.
The later Presentation Proposal lists three presentation models: Coliseum, Duel Club and the Surveillance System (CCTV). It arranges them as a proposed consecutive three-day experience. The models, schedule and spatial configuration in that document remain a proposal, rather than proof that every component was implemented.
The Final Solution page brings together assemblies, rules and reflective writing. The Duel Club page preserves its calls, event texts and images. Fictional world-building, records of particular events and later proposals retain their separate status.

2022 / Continuing workshops, relational practice and documentation
Romance Theatre
Shared exercises and lived encounters return through documentation to theatre.
He Fa’s role
Organisation and continuing practice, documented in his interview
Original proposal text
Liang Yin, 3 November 2022
Dated records
Recruitment and meeting records in November 2022; retrospective interview published November 2023
From proposal to continuing practice
In November 2022, Liang Yin published the call for Romance Theatre. The proposal asked participants to build relationships through group exercises, record lived encounters, derive a script from the recordings and eventually play themselves. A meeting article published on 6 November records the project’s initial gathering. Romance serves as a subject and brings participants into contact with their own and others’ expectations.
In an interview published in 2023, He Fa explicitly states that he was working on this project and describes continuing workshops roughly two or three times a week. Attendance was not fixed. Pandemic restrictions in November 2022 prevented some participants from attending, while others returned after restrictions eased. His account places the proposal’s schedule within lived circumstances: continuing work depends on the ability to meet and on individual wishes and practical conditions.
Proposal and archival reading
The nine-day rhythm, proposed relationship development and filming plan belong to the original method. This page considers the movement between theatre and life that the proposal sets out. Its claims about perceptual capacities and relationship outcomes remain claims made in the proposal, rather than verified effects.

The Rooftop Howler
From recruitment and rehearsal to performance: tracing how shared work takes form.
Documentation of The Rooftop Howler.
Image record & citation
hf-img-61c159659973
Close view of an open-mouthed figure in white
Between black title bars, a long-haired figure in a loose white shirt appears with their mouth open and the upper face cropped. Warm light catches the chest and fabric folds against darkness; the bars identify P4 Theater, the p4U programme and the work title.
HE FA’S ROLE
P4 organizing and 3P documentation
Year
2020–2021
Medium
Live theatre, rehearsal and moving-image record
Role
P4 organisation / 3P live documentation
Further reading
Howlers on the Rooftop performance details
↗
The project moved through casting and rehearsal in 2020 and was performed at P4 at 19:30 on 2 January 2021.
04
Project statement
Howlers on the Rooftop was developed through P4U, leaving open calls, rehearsal materials, participant texts, a public performance and later conversations. The performance took place at P4 at 19:30 on 2 January 2021.
Alongside his organisational work through P4, He Fa joined Zhang Shaohua and Huang Lucang in the 3P group’s live documentation.
A line through the work
When personal experience is rehearsed and heard by others, how does it become a public situation?
The theatre manager within the script
Page 9 of the retained Rooftop Howler script PDF names “He Fa” among the characters in Act Four, with that character responding to an interruption as the theatre manager. This is a role within the script: the document alone does not establish that He Fa performed in a particular show or wrote the script, and its fictional events should not be treated as real incidents. The filename’s designation “final playwright’s version” is a version label and does not establish that this text was used in a public performance.
Archival document supplement. Source: the retained PDF titled The Rooftop Howler (final playwright’s version), p. 9; title translated. The date of completion and playwright credit have not been verified. English is an editorial translation.
WORK WORLD / OPEN FROM HERE
Does participating in a work mean agreeing with it?
Close reading ↓
When can it end
Crossings ↗
CLOSE READING / 2026 CURATORIAL INTERPRETATION
The Rooftop Howler
Does participating in a work mean agreeing with it?
Work date: 2020–2021
Reading: 2026
Begin with what happens in the work
The archive contains recruitment, rehearsal, character texts, performance and post-performance interviews.
In a published interview, Qingyi says the unfamiliar open format strengthened his preference for conventional theatre; Reinate expresses dissatisfaction with the script and room for revision.
A character who keeps howling makes the fictional city ask what his voice means. Discussion around the production returns that question to its making: who can speak, whose views alter the structure, and who stays chiefly to complete the performance? The published interviews are valuable because they do not polish every experience into the same story of growth. Some value the company more than the script; others leave more certain that they want a different kind of theatre.
These disagreements are not decorative signs of authenticity. They test what openness actually enabled. Giving them a central place allows source material to resist the portfolio’s positive account. Yet one participant’s allegation about another person should not become an adjudicated fact. The accurate form retains who said what, when, and leaves room for further responses. Documentation gains value here by letting a work remain open to judgment after its performance ends.
The limits of this reading
Criticism in the interview is an attributed account, not a factual ruling by this site. Characters are not equated with their performers.
Sources for this reading
Based on performance records and the first Howler backstage interview, published 28 March 2021. Interviewees’ views retain their attribution.

2010 / Photography, archival pigment print
Sanhetan
Trees, snow and the waterside are assembled across the seams of separate photographs.
Sanhetan, 2010. Portfolio image 1 of 3.
Image record & citation
hf-img-e72ff973e668
Sanhetan: trees and paths in snow
A square montage combines snowy ground, bare trees and paths receding into the distance. Low stones and a curved bench punctuate the foreground. Overlapping rectangles of differently lit sky interrupt and repeat branches across the visible photographic joins.
Artist
He Fa
Date
February–April 2010
Recorded dimensions
520 × 520 mm
Recorded medium
Archival pigment print
Images and presentation
The portfolio records three square images for Sanhetan. In the first two, trees, snow, stones and structures are joined from rectangular photographs; blocks of different brightness remain visible in the sky. The third turns to the water and its edge: boats, pavilions, stone paths and waterbirds occupy different rectangular photographs. Visible seams continually disclose how the image has been assembled.
The fragments do not fully share a single perspective. Each image can be read as a scene or examined along its seams, one photographed object at a time. The title page dates the work to February–April 2010 and identifies it as an archival pigment print measuring 520 × 520 mm. The three images sit under one work entry; the source does not give them individual titles.
