Introduction: From Blueprint to Architecture
If the first part is a theoretical blueprint, the task of this chapter is to show how Regnault uses this blueprint to analyze the specific theatre "building". Regnault's critical practice is not a simple "subject analysis" or "person review". It is a structural diagnostics. Like a psychoanalyst, he listens to this "patient" phrase of the dramatic text, but his aim is not to understand the face of the phrase, but to identify the unconscious "symptoms", "slip of the tongue" and "rupture point" because it is in these places that the true desire and internal conflict of the text are revealed.
Regnault's case analysis usually focuses on a central issue: How is the theatre's "devices" specially adapted to produce the unique "gaze" effect and, ultimately, the form of "excitedness"? He's concerned about the unique "mutual economic model" of each piece.
"Every great drama is a unique desire machine. The Molière machine is a sophisticated, ironic social lens. Claudel's machine is an ambitious telescope that tries to capture sacred gaze. It is not the task of critics to judge the good or bad of these machines, but to reverse engineering (reverse-engineer) them and to reveal how their inner gears and levers work."
This chapter will select two key cases that Regnault has repeatedly referred to in his writings and articles - - Molière and Claudel - to demonstrate the concrete application of their critical methods. Subsequently, as an original contribution to this paper, we will try to activate and test the contemporary applicability of the Regnault doctrine by analysing a more contemporary dramatic phenomenon that may challenge its theory.
7.1 Molière: the dramatic breakdown of order
As we foreshadowed in chapter VI, Regnault's interpretation of Molière is the most representative example of its theoretical application. He saw the comedy of Molière, in particular its "comédies de caractère", as an experiment on how symbolic order was disturbed and subverted by an "other thing".
Case: Le Tartuffe
Theatrical setup: The whole play was set up in a rich middle-class family (the Orchon family). The family is a microcosm of the social symbol order, with its established rules, hierarchy and value system (represented by the voice of reason, Clement).
"Another"/ "Small pair a": Darduff. The danger of Tartuffe is not that he is a simple liar. His wisdom is that he is a perfect disguise. He does not "have" piety, but he is perfectly "playing" the symbol of piety. He used the "shell" that symbolized order (religious discourse) better than anyone, thus emptying its "nerves". Dalduff himself has become a walking, attractive "objet petit a", which has triggered a pathological desire (a homophobic obsession) and attracted the attention of the audience.
Caution: The audience experiences a double gaze when watching The Hypocrisy. On the one hand, they look at Darduff's hypocrisy from a God's perspective (as Al Quintow is hiding under the table) and get the pleasure of a "see through" trick. But on the other hand, they also felt a deeper "gaze" from the role of Tartuffe. This gaze seems to be laughing at the audience and society as a whole: "You see, the whole symbolic order on which you have maintained is so vulnerable that I can play it over the palms with only a few prayers and a few gestures."
Production of a sense of pleasure: The pleasure of the play is not from the last king ' s intervention and justice (which is only for the end of censorship, a forced stitch). True pleasure arises from the entire process of witnessing the imminent collapse of symbolic order. When Orghon gave Dalduf all his property, and when both law and reason seemed powerless, the audience experienced a dizziness of fear and excitement. Here, it's a defensive mechanism to deal with this traumatic perception. We laugh in order to hide our fears: the "real" of our world is so fragile.
Regnault's analysis raised the Hypocrisy from a simple moral sarcasm to a deep philosophical parable about the vulnerability of "real", "concealing" and symbolic order.
7.2 Paul Claudell: a noble call to the holy gaze
If Molière's plays are horizontal and social, Paul Claudel's plays go to school vertically. Regnault saw Claudel as an absolute, sacred playwright who tried to summon a dramatic device from the eyes of the big Other.
Case: Partage de Midi
Theatrical dispositifs: Theatrical language in Claudel is at the heart of their devices. This is an ambitious, poetic, religious and rhythm-filled verset claudélien. This language itself seeks to go beyond daily communication to become a container capable of carrying divine revelation. The scenery is usually symbolic and extremely simple and is intended to provide a ceremonial space for the language.
Desires and taboos: The story revolves around four people on a ship bound for China, centred on the unpermissible passion between married women Ysé and three men. This passion, especially the love between Ize and Mesa, has been portrayed as an absolute, destiny force that transcends secular morality. It is both an "alternative path" to God's love and a sin.
Claudell's play is no longer about a specific "objet petit a", but about the pervasive, silent, judging God. The characters struggle in passion, and every choice they make, every word they say, is as if they were reporting to God, trying to find a place for their existence in God's eyes. Audiences are invited to enter, not in a common sense of the role, but in a common experience of this situation of "godly eyes".
Joissance of the Sublime: what the viewers experience when they watch the Claudel drama is not a moribund sarcasm, but a kind of "the sublime" experience in the Kant sense. Faced with an incomprehensible, mountain-leaving poetic language and an absolute passion that transcends human ethics, the audience feels small and limited. This "infinite sense of oppression" was finally transformed into a painful and gruesome sense of pleasure. It is an extraordinary experience that is felt, mixed with piety and fear, when it is overwhelmed by a stronger power.
Regnault's analysis revealed the "theological-wigby" structure of the Claudel's drama. It is a machine that tries to turn the passion of human beings (Eros) into the thirst for sacred things (Agape), even though this road is filled with sin and punishment.
7.3 Contemporary theoretical application (original contribution): tracking out of control in immersion theatre
Regnault's theory was born in the whole period of the frame stage. So, is his theory still valid in the "fourth wall" completely destroyed contemporary immersive theatre? This constitutes the ultimate test of its doctrine.
Case analysis: Sleep No More from the British Punchdrunk
Theatrical dispositifs: this is a complete subversion of traditional devices.
Clear space: no fixed stage and audience. The whole play took place in a multi-storey building, and the audience was free to swim.
Anonymized viewers: The viewers are asked to wear a uniform white mask, which is more effective than darkness in removing personal identities and converting them into "$" in the sense of Regnault, anonymous and functional.
The promise of silence: the viewers are strictly forbidden to speak, making them pure, ghost-like spectators.
A Gaze Uncontrolled and Diffused: In traditional theatres, the sources of sight (stage) are clear. But in Sleep No More, the gaze became everywhere and thus out of control.
Multiple focus: At all times, multiple performances take place in different spaces. The audience is always in an anxiety of "missing out", which in itself drives their desires.
The actor's inverted gaze: the actor sometimes stops suddenly, grabs a masked audience and performs a one-on-one closely. At this moment, the audience suddenly turned from a voyeur to a subject. It is the strongest and most direct attack of "gaze", often with a devastating impact on the audience.
Audiences gaze at each other: masked viewers are also part of each other's landscape. You see other phantom masks moving around you, and you know that you are being observed. The entire space became a maze of mutual vision.
A new pattern of pleasure: pleasure in the production of immersion theatre, unlike Molière or Claudel. It's a loss of pleasure. Audiences continued to fail in their pursuit of storylines, eventually abandoning symbolic control over "complete narratives". Instead, they enjoy pure, mysterious, sensory experiences. This process of abandoning control and subjugating itself to the large and confusing logic of the device is itself a pleasure. You don't try to "understand", you just become part of the drama.
Conclusion: Regnault's theory, instead of being ineffective in the face of immersion theatre, shows an amazing interpretation. The immersion theatre can be seen as an extreme variant of the Regnault theatre "device". By deconstructing traditional devices, it creates a stronger and more ubiquitous desire capture system. It no longer requires a central stage to launch "observe", but rather to disperse "observe" throughout the environment, leaving the audience with no escape. It ultimately confirms Regnault's core argument: the essence of the drama is not in the story, but in the "mechanical device" that is carefully designed to shape the behaviour we see and the subject experience.
Part IV: Critical assessment and future outlook
Part IV: Critical Assessment and Future Prospects
Chapter 8: Internal tension and external criticism
Chapter 8: Internal Tensions and External Critiques
Introduction: The boundaries of a theory
François Regnault's Audience opened an unprecedented frontier for dramatic research with its theoretical purity, depth and system. It is, however, this extreme purity that constitutes the boundary of its doctrine and the potential "achilles". When we place this sophisticated Lacanian instrument in a broader theoretical spectrum and more diverse dramatic practice, a number of questions emerge: is its universality at the expense of historical particularities? Does its emphasis on structure unfairly suppress the emotional and physical dimensions? Does its seemingly neutral "gaze" mask the deep power politics behind it?
The purpose of this chapter is not to overthrow the theoretical building of Regnault, but to explore the strength of its heavy wall and to indicate where it may be necessary to strengthen or open new windows. We will engage in critical reflections from four key dimensions: first, to explore the tension between the generality of its theoretical model and its historical specificity; secondly, to engage in a dialogue with the increasingly important contemporary emotional theory (Affect Theory); again, to re-examine its concept of "gaze" from the perspective of feminism and post-colonialism; and finally, to reflect on the possible closedness and "theoretical hegemony" of its theoretical approach itself.
"The greatness of a theory is also reflected in the quality of criticism it triggers. Regnault's theory, like a steep mountain peak, provides us with an unparalleled vision, but climbing it, or even just walking around it, will make us aware of the existence of other paths and of the landscape that this mountain peak itself has hidden. Our mission is to paint these hidden landscapes."
8.1 Theoretical universality vs. History
Regnault's theoretical model has a strong universality across time and space. The "audience" position, the "device" function and the "gaze" mechanism he described seemed to apply equally to the ancient Greek open theatre, the Shakespeare Global Theatre and contemporary experimental black boxes. This generality is the source of its theoretical power, but it also constitutes its main potential shortcoming.
Is there a risk of levelling the huge historical, cultural and social differences between the ancient Greek citizens, the "grandlings" of the Elizabeth era and the contemporary middle-class audience being placed under the same abstract "$" symbol? Are the ritual, community and political functions of the ancient Greek drama really the same as the individualization, psychologicalization and commodification features of modern bourgeois theatres, the subjects called for by their "devices"?
The applicability of non-Western drama: Regnault's theory is almost entirely based on Western drama. Will this theory be "controversial" when confronted with dramatic traditions such as the Japanese can play, the Indian Brahma or the Chinese play, which have very different aesthetic principles, performance relationships and philosophical foundations? For example, the relationship between the audience (see box) and the performer (shower) is more based on a shared, highly programmed cultural memory and the aesthetics of the Unseen (yūgen) than on a Lacanian desire/miss model. The imposition of concepts such as "gaze" or "objet petit a" could result in theoretical and violent colonization.
Challenges of the digital age: In the age of YouTube live, VR dramas and TikTok dramas, traditional theatre "devices" are being dismantled and re-engineered. How will Lennon's theory based on physical co-presentation and dark closed space respond when the audience can stop, fast-track, and comment on the curtains, when the presence becomes replicable and delayed? Does that mean that we need a new, digital "module" that is more powerful than multi-economic?
Critical conclusion: Regnault's theory should perhaps be seen more as an in-depth analysis of a particular modern Western theatre device, modelled on the Italian frame stage, than a universal truth that is universal. Recognition of its historical limitations does not diminish its value, but rather allows us to better position our contribution.
Structure vs. Emotion vs. Act and the Body
Regnault's theory, as a typical product of French structuralism, is deeply sceptical about psychology and charisma, so it consciously excludes "emotion" and purely physical "sensation" from its core analysis. However, since the twenty-first century, accompanied by an "emotional turn", a growing number of theorists (e.g. Eve Sedgwick, Brian Massumi) have begun to emphasize the importance of "emotional" as a pre-linguistic, non-personal, inter-physical strength.
In Regnault's model, the audience's body is primarily a disciplined object, bound to a chair to catch it with ease. But emotional theory reminds us that the audience's body is also a positive "sonning board". Theatrical sounds, rhythms, light can directly affect the nervous system of the audience and trigger "emotional" reactions at the physical level (e.g., goose bumps, heart rate, muscle stress) that precede any conscious "understanding" or "identity".
The relationship between "emotional" and "favourable": the concept of "jouissance" in Regnault does touch upon the limit of the body. However, it is a devastating and extreme experience associated with "real-world" trauma. Emotional theory is more concerned with the non-destructive, building blocks of physical strength that flow in daily experience. The pleasure of a purely kinetic performance, or the resonance of a body triggered by a beautiful piece of music, can hardly be subsumed into the dualism of "plaisir" or "jouissance". They seem to point to another more powerful than a multi-economic model.
The return of the phenomenon: books such as Erika Fischer-Lichte's Performing Aesthetics have re-emphasized the performance as an "event" "self-generated feedback loop" (autopoeietic feedbackback loop). In this model, the energy of actors and viewers (whether physical or emotional) stimulates each other and creates the uniqueness of performance together. This is in stark contrast to Regnault's one-way "structural causal link", which is determined by the device.
Critical conclusion: Regnault's theory, because of its insistence on pure structure, may underestimate the dynamics of the body and the emotional flow of the former language in the dramatic experience. Future studies can combine Regnault's structural analysis with the physical analysis of emotional theory and explore how structures can guide and shape emotional flows, and how emotional outbreaks can in turn shock and change structures.
8.3 Conservative politics: cross-examination of feminism and post-colonial theory Question
Regnault's "le regard" is an abstract, seemingly neutral structural concept. However, since Laura Mulvey's landmark article, Visual Pleasure and Narrative Cinema, in 1975, we can no longer speak of a "gender-free" gaze.
The Male Gaze: Mulvey points out that in mainstream Hollywood films, cameras (the gaze of the dispositif), the eye of the male lead and the eye of the audience often conspire to portray the role of women as a passive, pornographic wonder. This "male gaze" is a manifestation of patriarchy. Regnault's theory, because of its emphasis on structural universality, does not fully explore whether "gaze" in theatre devices also has deep gender codes. When a naked woman's body is on stage, is it really just a neutral "objet petit a" working? Or does it activate a specific set of sexier economies that serve male viewers?
The Colonial Gaze: Similarly, post-colonial theories (such as Frantz Fanon, Edward Said) reveal the power role of "gaze" in colonial relations. Through their "gaze", the colonizers "otherize" the colonized people, portraying them as alien, primitive and in need of indoctrination. Is this colonial power relationship also inadvertently replicated when a Western theatre expresses alienity? Can Regnault's theory effectively analyse this racial and cultural politics that stares at us?
Critical conclusion: Regnault's "gaze" theory needs to be further politicized and contextualized. It is not enough to point to the existence of "gaze", but we must also ask: whose eyes is that? It serves whose power? The integration of Regnault's structural analysis with feminist and post-colonial power analysis would be a very productive direction for research.
8.4 Theoretical closedness and "theoretical hegemony"
Finally, we need to reflect on Regnault's methodology itself. A common criticism of Lacan psychoanalysis is that it is a closed system of high self-conformity and self-cycling. Any objection to, or lack of understanding of, the doctrine can be interpreted as a form of "resistance", thus further confirming its validity.
Unverifiable hypocrisy: is there a similar problem with Regnault's theory? It seems that any dramatic phenomenon can be "explained" by its terms. A success story is the success of the device in producing pleasure; a failure is the failure of the device. Is this force of interpretation an expression of its deepness or a symbol of its cyclical justification?
The threshold of terminology: Regnault's writing is highly dependent on Lacan's terminology, which, while building on its theoretical rigour, sets a very high reading threshold, which could lead to a "elitist word" that only a few "in-circles" can master, thereby excluding other critical voices.
Critical conclusion: In using Regnault doctrine, we must maintain a methodological vigilance. It should be seen as a powerful "detection light" rather than as a "one-size-fits-all key" to explain everything. It can light up some of the dark corners of the theatre, but we must also realize that the stronger the beam it throws, the deeper the shadow around it.
Conclusion
Reaffirming the core argument: a paradigm shift in theory
The core argument of this paper is that the book " Audience ", published by François Regnault in 1986, is not a simple addition or amendment to the theatrical theory, but a fundamental paradigm shift (paradigm Shift). It shifts irreversibly the centre of dramatic research from the "re-emerging content" of the stage to the invisible but decisive structure of desire between the stage and the audience. By carrying out a systematic "theory shift" in Jacques Lacan's psychoanalytic theory, Regnault has accomplished a seemingly impossible task: He found a non-psychological, non-sociological and purely structural basis for theatre theory.
Our research shows that this "Regnault revolution" was achieved through a series of theoretical operations that were rounded up
Audience "de-centre" and "structured": Regnault uses "audience" from an active, psychologically deep, empirical individual to "clean up" a "empty position" ($) of the `functional, algebraic type' foreseen by the dramatic "dispositif". The essence of this position is the "manque" in the sense of Lacan, which drives desire, not emotion or reason, to become the fundamental driving force for the audience to enter the theatre.
Theater's "mechanized": Regnault has recast the theatre as a sophisticated and Althusserian ideological "dispositif". Through architecture, social contracts and aesthetic technology, the machine calls and instructs audiences, and its ultimate strategic objective is to systematically capture and direct libido.
At the heart of "gaze": the archstone of Regnault's theory is his brilliant application of the concept of le regard. He argued convincingly that the essence of the drama was not "seeing", but how the audience was captured as "objet petit a" from the scene. The magic of the theatre stems from the moment when the subject feels divided and fascinated in the experience of "watching".
The ultimate goal of "jouissance": ultimately, Regnault points to the culmination of the theatre experience from the traditional aesthetic "plaisir" to the Lacanian "jouissance". It is a painful and excessive enjoyment that comes when there is a symbolic breakdown in order and when the Real break in. The greatest drama is not intended to appease, but to push the audience to the edge of the fragmentation of the subject.
By analysing the case studies of Molière, Claudel and even contemporary immersion theatres, this paper validates the strong interpretation of the doctrine in critical practice. It penetrates the dramatic images of different times and different styles, revealing the deep structures of desire, disguise, missing and obscuring beneath it.
In short, François Regnault's " Audience " forces us to confront a permanent and profound question: What happens when we watch? His answers were complex, subversive and sometimes disturbing. He told us that, in what seemed to be a safe darkness in the theatre, we were involved in a dangerous game about how our own subjectivity was constructed, divided and driven by desire. We thought we were the kings who went to the play, but finally found that we were just sitting on an empty throne crowned with "gaze".
The work of this paper is to try to understand the configuration of this throne, to trace its blueprints and to assess the shadows of its glory. And perhaps the ultimate significance of this work is that it will allow us to walk into the theater the next time the lights go out, with a new, more conscious sense of consciousness about what is about to begin, about ourselves.

P4 Theater and You
2025-06-11
Project and brand narrative
Chen Jianli｜"Shi Shuo"
The heavens bear witness that if the sun sheds tears, self-esteem will melt like bad ice cream, and some souls will be haunted by nightmares for a long...
The heavens bear witness that if the sun sheds tears, self-esteem will melt like bad ice cream, and some souls will be haunted by nightmares for a long time. When the music played from the loudspeaker, the hound-like teenagers identified the direction on the dusty playground and rushed to their respective positions. On another special day, in addition to preaching about the great situation, the principal also reviewed the school's glorious school history: In 1929, Sun Zhen, deputy commander of the 29th Army of the People's Liberation Army, generously donated money to run the school. In a few years, one of the best private schools in the country was built in the southwest corner of the country (from Huang Yanpei, a red educator recognized by great men). In order to comply with the general trend that blood is thicker than water and love is as deep as the sea on both sides of the Taiwan Strait, with the approval of the authorities, the school name "Shude" was restored... I was distracted and caught a glimpse of the gray teaching building on the left, with bullet holes from the X-Men wars vaguely visible on the outer wall. I remembered the old teacher saying that gunfire was constant during the day, and the building was full of earth-made stumbling landmines, and I couldn't help but shudder. The hardened soil on the soles of the feet seemed to become moist, and a group of duck-voiced sex sects escorted the shaved teacher around the playground. The teacher fell down, and they picked her up and continued running, and then dragged her on the ground. Whips, wooden sticks, and slaps were flying. The teacher was held down on her head and drank water from the mire... The amplification effect of the big speaker was not stable, and the principal's voice turned into an old capon.
Compared with history, the more specific sense of oppression comes from senior boys. They carry cigarettes, daggers and muscles on their bodies, and they talk all about "Taipei is not my home, and my hometown has no neon lights." They may rush in front of you at any time, twist your neck, and lower their voices: "Young man, borrow some money to spend" - I hope this is just a delusion of persecution. One afternoon in the second grade of junior high school, I had just locked my bicycle when a chair smashed through the roof of the carport, fell from the sky, and landed on my head. At that time, my vision went dark, and I suddenly felt that the end was coming. It took me a long time to recover. I didn't tell anyone about it afterward, because I knew no one would investigate the cause for me, except my parents, but I didn't want to add to their worries. Fortunately, this compromised disaster did not damage my intelligence, but my head seemed to be harder.
If one had to choose an image for the horrors of adolescence, it would undoubtedly be him: Chen, the head teacher of the third year of junior high school, a mathematics teacher. Later, no matter where I heard people talking about the 1980s like a white-headed palace maid talking about Xuanzong, I was somewhat disdainful, because I was not forgetful. I used the scraper of memory to carve out many details of the barbarism, vulgarity and vulgarity that were characteristic of the times, and I dared to take responsibility for my disapproval of its integrity. The children of X government officials, X team cadres, and state-owned enterprise bosses can enter the school without test score restrictions. Those who spend money to enter are called "Qian Xuesen," or "money students." Whenever the school boasted that Pan Wenhua, Sun Zhen's boss, had failed in his attempt to get his son and nephew to join the school, it was like a slap in the face. From the privacy of campus to the surrounding streets, bullying is everywhere. "I'll give your baby some blood!" is the mantra of young bullies. This stinking world is no less impressive than the lower class society in Peking described by Lao She. But for me, it is not the most dangerous nightmare, because I can't get rid of Chen's dehydrated kidney bean face all year round.
Chen has a withered body, a hale and hearty spirit, and protruding eyes, showing good thyroid function. He graduated from a junior college class at Chengdu University. He claims to be very familiar with Western classical music and has a large collection of imported tapes. However, in my impression, he has never hummed a complete melody without being off-key. The bad relationship between me and Chen started with a small dispute: he asked the whole class to copy the theorems in the mathematics textbook ten times, otherwise the class would not be dismissed. I dared to raise objections. Chen suddenly became furious, and the twelve-year-old me advised him not to get angry... From that day on, I fell into purgatory. It was no longer possible to have friends. Any classmate who played with me would be suppressed by Chen. If we did not break off the friendship immediately, he would take the time to visit the parents and warn their parents with a savior-like authority: Don't play ball with him, don't pick up on his comments, avoid him and go home. Your son will hopefully go to college. All class cadres and students who pursue progress have the responsibility to supervise my words and deeds and report to Chen. However, he prefers to peek at my every move through the crack in the classroom door. Then he suddenly leans out half of his body and yells at me who is talking with gritted teeth: You can run away, you are a fool! I pay tribute to Mr. Chen, who took the trouble to intensify and train my practical writing skills, and forced me to write self-reflection letters day after day, also called inspection, and sometimes called "understanding". In the past three years, I have accumulated at least four to five hundred copies! I gradually learned to enjoy the process of the pen tip sliding, rising and falling on the paper. The sense of absurdity slowly grew, and sometimes it seemed as if I could look down on myself from the ceiling. Most people laugh at bad luck as part of bad luck, bad luck is part of compulsory education, and compulsory education is part of non-violent non-cooperation. Chen also hated me extremely for playing table tennis after school. Once I was caught playing table tennis, the racket and net would take his surname. He has a habit of pretending to leave school and then come back to make sure everyone gets the stolen goods.
Once again, I pay tribute to Chen. Without his careful design, I would not have been able to experience the feeling of being convicted for literary crimes with my minor body and mind. One day, Mr. Chen called me to his office and mysteriously asked me to write an article, using a physics teacher who continued to work despite being ill as the protagonist, to highlight the selfless dedication of people's teachers. The key point was to express the current situation that intellectuals in transition are generally short-changed in terms of material rewards, and strive to attract the attention of various industries. After I finished writing this essay, Chen had another handle on me. He threatened with a serious face: The school leaders read your article and agreed that there is a problem with your ideological tendency, and it is not a small problem! I forgot to defend myself and only saw him talking wildly. When I walked out of the office, I couldn't help but want to vomit, and I retched several times. Several years later, Situ Zhaodun once told me that Xia, the only witness of his father Situ Huimin's latent work at a certain stage, refused to testify. Situ Huimin said: He wants my life. In another context, my life or death may be uncertain. However, the narrative that lacks innovation is plagiarized in another time and space, and the destructive intensity is not satisfactory. I despise Chen for inheriting the mantle of persecution. His behavior is as dirty as maggots fluttering in a dry toilet, but Breaking the Sky has only developed into a fable full of loopholes, or a joke like water-filled pork.
How to describe Chen's good intentions and deep affection for me, like Shakespeare, comparing it to a summer day? He frequently advised me to drop out of school and stop being a bad guy. When he saw that I kept my head down and said nothing, he offered to take a step back and send me to a work-study school. Chen even expressed that he would rather use his social connections to contact me on his behalf. It's hard to overestimate his power of action. If I had been replaced by another person of the same age, his helpless parents would probably suffer the loss of a life. Just driving people crazy and stupid would be considered merciful. Perhaps only Stanislavsky understood Chen's supreme mission, like the legendary trafficker stuffing the abducted boy into a bottle? Use a hard container to prevent his body from growing and at the same time create a deformed, big-headed doll? Unfortunately, my nerves are getting stronger day by day, and my body is getting stronger day by day. Before I was fifteen years old, I was more than half a head taller than Chen. I could run 100 meters in under 12 seconds, do thirty pull-ups in one go, and I was not afraid when I met the senior classmate with a sinister face - Literature? Art? Family affection? friendship? To be precise, all beautiful things gave me the strength to overcome being bullied by ugly people. I spent my spare time in Xinhua Bookstore, foreign language bookstore and ancient book bookstore, absorbing nutrients from the rhymes of Yang Xiong, Sima Xiangru, Chen Ziang, Li Bai, Du Fu, Li He and Li Shangyin, and from Thomas Hood, John Keats, Wordsworth, Bo The writings of Mrs. Ronning, Longfellow and "The Rubaiyat" are open-minded, and I seek the courage to resist violence and insult from the heroes of "Three Heroes of Swords", "Seven Heroes of Five Righteousness", "Little Five Righteousness" and "Continued Little Five Righteousness", and enter into "Selected Works", "Parallel Style Wenchao", "Ten Thousands of Tang Dynasty Quatrains" and "Complete Tang Poems" to collect my fragile but refusing to be mediocre dream...
Idioms are my best friends, such as "Besieged on all sides", "The road is as wide as the eyes", "Please enter the urn", and "Keep your mouth shut." But occasionally I would use the rules of the game to be wild. I liked to say eloquently in front of the student cadres sent by Chen to monitor me: "Chen, I'm going to let you go!" One of the Youth League branches, S secretary Wu, whose parents were teachers at the provincial school of I rode a bicycle from the Meteorological College where my father taught, passed through the iron gate of the Fourth Supervisor, and entered the middle school. I said goodbye to Chen's amateur performance scene and went straight to the ancient book bookstore shaded by green trees behind the lonely bronze statue of Sun Yat-sen on Chunxi Road. After bending down to read for a long time, I often feel briefly dizzy when I look up. The colorful book titles dance, and the world begins to fluctuate, following a gentle curve. In a trance, an old gentleman with white hair and beard bowed to another old gentleman: Brother, when I was in Oxford... the city has completely degraded through demolition, and physical landmarks with humanistic value are always the first to die. And I will always miss my Chinese teacher, Mr. Huang Zhenru, I want to show him the poems and dramas I wrote, the movies I made, the magazines I edited, and talk about the unexpected eminent monks and adulterous monks, the sage and the demonic, the academics and the scoundrels, the aristocrats and the rich businessmen who intentionally or unintentionally offended, the gentlemen and the villains, the gangsters and the magicians...
It has been almost thirty years since Mr. Huang left this world, and I seem to be getting closer and closer to his literature-obsessed, sincere love and hate heart. There were so many cold or humid evenings that we rode together, because there were endless names like Xu Wei, Fu Shan, Wang Duo, and He Shaoji. I would send him to the door of my house, but he was not satisfied and sent me home again. Along the way, we commented on the writing methods of old and new signboards along the way, appreciated the writing power and skillful skills of old craftsmen, and brought out the unique wretchedness of the officials of the Book Association. The old stories he told always had a different meaning. For example, after the X-creator sect ransacked the house and only left a set of Wang Li's "Ancient Chinese", Teacher Huang was puzzled. Later, an expert reminded: The Chinese X-literary also had a Wang Li with the same name. Going to school is a long-lasting punishment, but if you grit your teeth and hold on, there is hope that "it will be beneficial to you." Everything I love is encouraged and blessed by Teacher Huang. Reading, memorizing, and chanting allow the "Book of Songs" and "Chu Ci" to penetrate into my blood, and understand Shakespeare and Tagore in different styles. He gave me a copy of "Tian Wen" in small regular script and told others: Chen Li loved Qu Yuan the most. "Huang Sheng is fond of reading poetry, and he works hard to find out. He is often shy about making statements, but he is unwilling to make promises. Sometimes he gets a witty saying, and it is as fast as unlocking a key. He is full of energy, and he is just a new leader. How he has endured the hard times and ten years of turmoil. Although he has been worried about the dangers, his ambition is to write..." This is a poem written by Mr. Lu Jianyu, another erudite scholar in our school, to Mr. Huang. I would like to bow to the spirits of the two teachers in heaven.
That day, Mr. Chen made a fuss and kicked me out of school. I had a fever when I got home. When grandma went to ask me for sick leave, she met Teacher Huang first. He said that no one had the right to deprive students of their freedom to attend class. Chen didn't panic and told his grandmother: "Chen Li's condition is serious, but we have not given up on saving him. We are going to hold a meeting soon. I will chair it and invite teachers from all subjects, parent representatives and all class cadres to participate. How about treating the disease and saving lives?", everyone worked together to give him advice, find the root cause of the disease, prescribe prescriptions, and administer strong medicine. Chen Li made good notes and wrote a written guarantee to make corrections within a time limit and not to abandon himself to the collective. "It is a pity that Chen has an eye for gold and jade, and his grandmother is a veteran of Xinhai. The only daughter who attended Aurora University Law School immediately retorted: "It's feasible, but it must be reported to the school committee and the Chengdu Municipal Education Bureau, and reporters from daily newspapers, evening newspapers and TV stations are invited to cover the whole process. It has been more than ten years since the end of the Cultural Revolution, and you are very But if you do not reflect deeply and still engage in great criticism, it will harm the future of the motherland. It is indeed time to attract the attention of the whole society." Chen was stunned, and his grandmother walked away with a parting message: Wouldn't it be great to teach the world's talents? After a while, the whole class was going to Pujiang for an autumn trip to Chaoyang Lake and planned to stay one night. Chen did not allow me to participate. Teacher Huang interceded on his behalf and hit a snag. Chen said that if he went, the whole class would cancel the event. Teacher Huang comforted me: When the time comes, you can follow me on the station wagon. I hope he will be too embarrassed to kick us both out. I didn't go, but I remember Teacher Huang's kindness deeply.
Many years later, I was making tea with a couple around the stove. The female director sitting across from me was planning to make a documentary about "A Hundred Years of Film", and she asked a senior filmmaker named Yimi to have a drink in the evening. I said half-jokingly
"I'm just worried that I can't find this scumbag."
"Why do you say that?"
"He and I went to the same elementary school and middle school, and we have known each other for a long time."
"It goes without saying that my father is the founder of X and country X, and the secretary of X committee."
"I know that from Experimental Primary School to Ninth Middle School, his grades have been ranked last in the grade for more than ten years. He is semi-literate."
"But they rewrote the film history of Country X."
"I know that he is the leader of the XX East Ideological Fighting Team of Ninth Middle School, or Jiumao for short. I also know that the day before, he was eating at the teacher's house and making up lessons. The next day, he picked up X, beat the teacher with a belt, and pooped in the human rice vat."
The most absurd situation in the world is that what you consider an unforgivable crime may be as trivial to others as urinating in a swimming pool or letting go of sex in a bus, which highlights the cuteness of the person with the red X's hormonal leakage. I remembered that Teacher Huang mentioned that one of his students was the son of Li Jingquan. He personally said that Li Zhitai dyed his head red with the blood of millions of Sichuan people. After taking a closer look at the lady opposite, I felt sad.
The small gathering broke up unhappy. Afterwards, the female director described to a mutual friend that I looked murderous at that time. Amitabha, it is undeniable that I am often angry because of worry, or worried because of anger. Chen was awarded the title of special teacher as he wished, and served as the vice principal and superintendent of a middle school, living and drinking until he retired. Compared with the wolves, tigers and leopards in this land, he is not even worthy of a bed bug. Teacher Huang's soul returned to Daoshan prematurely, so he could be considered safe. I look into my heart in the clear night, and I have an indescribable admiration for them. Teacher Huang has carried the noble character of a scholar throughout his life. He secretly followed Song Yi Fangjia, fearing to follow in the footsteps of Qi Liang. If the earth cannot be maintained and the pillars of heaven cannot be upheld, people will eat each other and lead beasts to eat people, or the world will be chaotic, good and evil will be indistinguishable, slanderers will be arrogant, and wise men will be nameless. He should be self-disciplined and self-respected according to his wishes as an elder. His life of being wronged and humiliated by mediocrity taught me that dignity comes with a price, it is extremely expensive. And Chen Mou is actually my superior condition for reverse growth, the so-called Bodhisattva of the Crossing Bodhisattva. He tried too hard to explain to me all the despicable aspects of the official education system, lamenting that he was punching and kicking me even in my dreams. His words and deeds prove that there is no freedom, fairness or even security in Dongsheng China. As a human being, if you don't cherish light, you may commit yourself to darkness. As for the middle ground of dark gray, light gray, flesh-colored, and pink, its legitimacy lies in stifling all scientific, artistic, or academic innovation. It is reminiscent of the performance of "The Master and Margarita" at the Masterskaya Theater in St. Petersburg this summer in Shanghai. Afterwards, a group of local experts were arranged to discuss the show. Director Kozlov sits among this group of theater laymen, dwarfs and imbeciles to receive praise and criticism. Does he expect to be led by the devil to fly? I just want to say: evil! What to say! When our self-consciousness and aesthetic attitude awaken, we may conflict with that kind of destructive violent machine or appendage at any moment. In modern society, tangible and intangible destruction is a daily coercion, and its density has increased due to the abundance of communication methods. How could I downplay how hurtful it was? How can we let it go unchecked? Fortunately, until now I still have the strength to stand, breathe, think, and sort out my position. I have given in, I may still give in, and I have been defeated by sadness countless times, but not at this moment. At this moment, I want to declare my position, my position, to every person or elf who has the patience to listen to me, using my tarnished and hammered language.
During the graduation season of junior high school, Chen did not change his true nature as a literary and artistic person, and gave each person in the class two lines of old poetry. What he gave me was "To be complacent in wine is to learn too much, and to be ungrateful in poetry is to be ungrateful." The taste of reading it today is slightly different from that of the past. First of all, I understood the hostility that travels through time and space. Cause and effect are clear. Seek kindness and get kindness. Don't be happy or fearful. Furthermore, my unique will has given me the strength to build a spiritual fortress, and I am eager to share this journey with tears, sweat, blood and laughter through poetry, prose, drama or images. Third, borrow a sentence from Dr. Johnson's letter to the Earl of Chesterfield: I have a stable mind and cannot be deceived by you; I have escaped from ghosts and cannot be damaged by you; I am full of Dharma joy and can discuss with the envoy. Using Buddhism's concept of turning consciousness into wisdom, you might as well read your curse, treat it as an ambiguous and meaningful prayer, and smile.

P4 Theater and You
2025-03-16
Theory and method
P4 Theater
Group Theory from a Psychoanalytic Perspective: Deleuze, Guattari, and Historical Context
An introduction to Group Theory from a Psychoanalytic Perspective: Deleuze, Guattari, and Historical Context, connecting P4 Theater, psychoanalysis, Lacan...
psychoanalysis theory has experienced many changes and developments since Freud was founded. Among them, the formation of group psychoanalysis theory represents an important expansion of the psychoanalysis field. This report will explore the historical context of group theory from the perspective of psychoanalysis, focusing especially on the theoretical contributions of Gilles Deleuze and Félix Guattari and their contemporary practice status, revealing the profound impact of this theoretical development on contemporary society.
The historical turn from classic psychoanalysis to schizophrenia analysis
Limitations of traditional psychoanalysis
The traditional psychoanalysis theory began with Freud, and its core feature is the obsession with the "three": the mind model of consciousness, subconsciousness and unconsciousness; the personality structure of id, ego and superego; and the triangular relationship between parents and children. As the search results show, this "principle of threes" is particularly prominent in the Oedipus complex, forming a "stable structural model that maintains patriarchal authority." In fact, this model often turns into a bipolar relationship and forms a static theoretical framework.
Freud and his followers attempted to develop psychoanalysis into a "science" in an attempt to discover the universal structure of the mind. However, this pursuit of universality has gradually revealed its limitations, especially in dealing with collective consciousness and social behavior. Traditional psychoanalysis is inherently individual-centered and has difficulty explaining group phenomena and social-level psychodynamics.
The rise of schizophrenia
It is against this background that the collaboration between Deleuze and Guattari opened up a new theoretical path. Guattari's identity as a psychoanalysis scholar precedes his identity as a philosopher. He "intervened in contemporary philosophy by engaging in psychoanalysis studies." Deleuze and Guattari met for the first time in 1969, marking the beginning of a remarkable collaboration. Deleuze had just completed two important works, "Difference and Repetition" and "The Logic of Sense," but he was not completely satisfied with his theoretical framework.
This collaboration resulted in the theory of "schizophrenia" (Schizoanalysis), which is different from Lacan's structuralism, but a critical transcendence of the traditional psychoanalysis. Schizophrenia analysis "is no longer about making the schizoid person suffer again in order to face a perverted normal world, but about reorienting the flow of libido in schizoanalysis." This shift fundamentally changed the goals and approach of psychoanalysis.
Theoretical Framework and Innovation of Deleuze and Guattari
The shift in thinking from structure to machine
Deleuze's early thought was deeply influenced by structuralism, but he always maintained a complex relationship with it. Through his collaboration with Guattari, Deleuze achieved a shift in thought from "structure" to "machine". Guattari's practical experience and critical thinking about Lacan provided Deleuze with a new perspective to overcome the limitations of structuralism.
This collaboration enabled Deleuze "to obtain a new psychoanalysis theory (Schizoanalysis, schizophrenia analysis), which no longer seeks to explain everything from the assumption of original repression, but to explain repression itself from a broader social perspective." This shift means a fundamental change in psychoanalysis's research objects and methods, from focusing on the "global-molar" self and id to a variety of local-molecular selves and desires.
A political analysis of desire and power
Anti-Oedipus and A Thousand Plateaus, the masterpieces of Deleuze and Guattari's collaboration, raise a core question: "Why do people tenaciously strive for their enslavement as if it is their salvation?" This question reveals the political dimension of their theory, that is, the relationship between desire and power.
Their reinterpretation of desire is a fundamental subversion of Freud's and Lacan's theories. In traditional psychoanalysis, desire is often defined as lack, while Deleuze and Guattari regard desire as productivity and a creative energy. This re-understanding of desire provides a new perspective for analyzing social power structures.
Basic propositions of schizophrenia analysis
Deleuze and Guattari's schizophrenia analysis has several key claims
1. They refuse to accept repression and castration as universal concepts. They believe that the concept of castration implies that there is only one gender - male, and that female is defined as lacking.
2. They proposed a "molecular" model of the unconscious, arguing that the unconscious knew nothing about castration. In their view, castration is an ideological construct rather than a unifying concept.
3. They believe that the unconscious produces multiplicity and fluidity, with "n genders...one hundred thousand." This led them to argue that even for Freud the unconscious was associated with static representations rather than with the production of myths, tragedies and dreams.
4. They propose that Oedipus is not just an ideological explanation of psychological functions, but the hegemonic limiting system of Western culture. Therefore, they advocate a "post-Oedipal" world.
Group therapy practice and the application of schizophrenia analysis
Laborde Clinic Practice
Guattari's work at the psychiatric clinic of La Borde was an important site for the practice of schizophrenia. There he "practiced schizophrenia with his patients". Guattari's attempt to avoid a hierarchical relationship between analyst and patient reflects the political dimension of schizophrenia analysis.
The group component of schizophrenia allows the analysis of "social machines and abstract expression assemblages that form subjectivity." This approach differs from the traditional psychoanalysis individual orientation and focuses more on social relationships and group dynamics. Guattari believed that group analysis could avoid the hierarchical relationship between analyst and patient, thereby creating a more equal and liberating therapeutic environment.
Challenges in practice
It is important to note, however, that schizoanalysis "was never designed as a therapeutic technique, and there are no clinical training courses or technical guidelines." This makes schizoanalysis face many challenges in practice. Guattari's own work at the Laborde Clinic was not always smooth, with his colleagues often annoyed by his "total inability to follow the rules."
Furthermore, the theoretical complexity and politics of schizoanalysis make it difficult to gain widespread acceptance within the traditional mental health system. Nonetheless, some elements of it have permeated various psychotherapeutic practices, particularly those that focus on group dynamics and social context.
Contemporary Development and Theoretical Influence
Crossover with other schools of psychology
Although schizophrenia has not become a mainstream treatment method, many of its ideas resonate with other psychological schools, including "existential psychology, humanistic psychology, feminism/postcolonialism/critical social theory", etc. These intersections demonstrate that the ideas of Deleuze and Guattari have transcended the scope of psychoanalysis and influenced broader social and cultural theory.
In particular, their critique of traditional psychoanalysis concepts of gender provides important resources for feminist psychology. They challenged the male-centered theory of castration and advocated the plurality of gender and desire, which has many resonances with contemporary gender theory.
Political Philosophy and Social Criticism
The theories of Deleuze and Guattari have had a profound impact on political philosophy. Their work "emerges from a combination of Freudian-Lacanian psychoanalysis__ and Marxist political economy" to form "a philosophy that views the world through the lens of desire."
This perspective provides a powerful tool for analyzing contemporary social and political phenomena. For example, their theory can help understand how capitalism maintains its dominance by manipulating desires, and why people sometimes support social structures that appear to go against their interests. Their ideas continue to play a role in current social movements and political criticism.
Contemporary applications of Deleuze-Guattari thought
Deleuze and Guattari's ideas have a variety of contemporary applications. In the political realm, their theories are used to analyze nationalism, capitalism, and neo-imperialism. The "middle class theory" perspective borrows part of the ideological framework of Deleuze and Guattari to analyze the dynamics of the ruling class in socialist society.
In art and cultural studies, their concepts such as "body without organs" and "desire machine" are used to analyze contemporary art, film and literature. The ideas of Deleuze and Guattari have also influenced new media studies and digital cultural analysis, especially discussions of identity, virtual reality, and digital society.
The state of contemporary grouppsychoanalysis practice
Institutionalization and academicization
Although schizophrenia has not formed a strict therapeutic system like traditional psychoanalysis, the ideas of Deleuze and Guattari have gained an important position in the academy. Their works are widely read and discussed in fields such as philosophy, cultural studies, sociology, and political theory.
However, this academicization also runs the risk that their anti-establishment critical thinking may become institutionalized and tamed. The work of Deleuze and Guattari is often simplified or taken out of context, potentially diminishing its revolutionary potential. As the search results warn, one may "pick out convenient quotations from the work of Deleuze and 'Deleuze-Guattari' to fill out a false image of 'political Deleuze'".
Acceptance and Development in China
In China, Guattari's ideas have been introduced for more than ten years. "Chaos Interpenetration" is Guattari's last book before his death, and it is also the first translation and introduction of Guattari's works in the Chinese world. The publication of this book and the positive response from readers indicate that Chinese readers have a strong interest in the thoughts of Deleuze and Guattari.
Chinese scholars have also begun to explore the integration of Deleuze and Guattari's ideas with Chinese cultural and social background. For example, some scholars have connected the theories of Deleuze and Guattari with social changes and political dynamics in China, exploring their applicability and limitations in the Chinese context.
Conclusion
Deleuze and Guattari's schizophrenia theory marks a major turn in the field of psychoanalysis. It not only challenges the traditional psychoanalysis theoretical framework, but also expands psychoanalysis's social and political dimensions. By viewing desire as a productive force rather than a lack, they offer new perspectives for understanding individuals and society. Although schizoanalysis did not develop into a standardized treatment approach, its ideas have permeated multiple disciplines and influenced contemporary thinking about subjectivity, power, desire, and social change. The collaboration between Deleuze and Guattari created a unique theoretical language that continues to inspire new thought and practice today.
In contemporary society, with the development of globalization, digitalization and new forms of social control, the ideas of Deleuze and Guattari appear increasingly relevant. Their theories of desire, power, and resistance provide important tools for analyzing current societies and open up space for imagining the possibilities of different social forms. As they show, we are all divided, and nothing psychoanalysis can bring us back to a unified self that simply does not exist. This insight remains deeply explanatory and transformative in today's divided and complex world.

P4 Theater and You
2025-03-09
Theory and method
Human Surrender
P4 Theater: The Generation and Reconstruction of an Experimental Art Space
A concise reconstruction of P4 Theater as an experimental art space, tracing its method, history, and public-facing practice.
P4 Theater: The generation and reconstruction of an experimental art space
Research on theater ecology based on interdisciplinary practice and social participation
Introduction
P4 Theater (P4 Theater), as a representative of China's contemporary independent experimental theater, has built an experimental space that combines the functions of creation, performance and social healing with the cross-border positioning of "photography-theater-sculpture-art" as its core since its establishment in 2015. This article explores its uniqueness and enlightenment in the contemporary art ecology by sorting out its development history, core concepts, artistic practice and social impact.
1. Core Concept: From "Organic Nature" to "Symbiotic Theater"
Tracing the Origin: The Dialectical Relationship between Photography and Reality
P4 Theater originally originated from the founder's reflection on "performance and reality" in photography. He believes that traditional photography often falls into the dilemma of "the subject and the photographer acting each other out", while theater, through its immediacy and interactive space, can stimulate "organic subconscious creation" and capture the true emotions hidden in the acting. This concept combines the instantaneity of photography with the dynamics of drama to form a unique "psychological depth reproduction" methodology.
Space Philosophy: Metaphors of the Black and White World
The theater divides the space into black and white poles through black velvet curtains: the black area symbolizes the "open heart" (stage and private studio), and the white area represents "gazing eyes" (auditorium and public space). The two are both divided and integrated, just like the rotating double figures in its logo, metaphorizing the dynamic reconstruction of the viewing and performance relationship. This design not only breaks the physical boundaries of traditional theaters, but also guides participants from "darkness to light" through an immersive experience, achieving psychological healing.
Social mission: classless publicity
P4 Theater emphasizes that "everyone is the protagonist of life" and advocates the elimination of class thresholds for artistic participation. The "you" in its slogan "photo for you" does not refer to a specific individual, but to everyone's repressed true self. This concept is practiced through open recruitment, improvisation and public participation projects (such as "psychological photography" and "live role-playing"), turning drama from "viewing" to "life-based intervention".
2. Development process: from black box to "generated university"
Start-up period (2015-2016): the foundation of experimental theater
In June 2016, P4 Theater opened at the Sculpture Terrace Art District in Beijing. The premiere of the experimental drama "Shadow Counterpoint" attracted attention. This work explores the narrative possibilities of interweaving reality and reality through a "spatial montage" of images, bodies and sounds. At this time, the theater is positioned as a cross-border laboratory that integrates venues and systems, accommodating multiple functions such as drama, film, and resident art.
Expansion period (2017-2021): iteration of rules and methods
With the launch of projects such as "Hamlet Mirror" and "Pixel Echo", p4 has gradually established a "recruitment-creation-performance" cycle system. Its signature project "p4U Project" has incubated works such as "Real Image" and "Cocoon House" through open recruitment of non-professional participants, emphasizing "extracting collective memory from individual stories." In 2021, due to the relocation of the venue to Wanghua Road, the theater space has been reduced but its experimental nature has become stronger. "510 Space" has become an incubator for new practices.
Transformation Period (2022-2025): Social Experimentation and Community Building
In projects such as "Purple Action" and "Duel Club", p4 turns to more critical social practices, such as exploring power structures, gender issues and the democratization of art. The founder He Fa proposed "theatre as a generative university" and advocated connecting strangers through drama and building a "close community that releases subtext." In 2025, the tenth anniversary of the theater, its methodology has been extended to films, workshops and public events, forming a two-way penetration network of "art-society".
3. Art practice: cross-border experimentation and participatory creation
Theater production: deconstruction from text to space
P4 Theater's works often break the traditional narrative framework. For example, "Shadow Counterpoint" uses musical counterpoint to structure the plot, creating "double viewing" through gauze projection and real-time images; "Human Surrender" uses psychoanalysis as a tool to deconstruct the power relationship between individuals and collectives. The stage design emphasizes "nomadic nature" and has been performed in non-traditional spaces such as parks, ruins, and office buildings, strengthening the intertextuality of environment and narrative.
Methodological Innovation: psychoanalysis and the Rules of Improvisation
The theater integrates psychoanalysis theory into creation, such as "subconscious improvisation" and "emotional catalyst" mechanisms. In the "p4U" project, participants need to excavate personal trauma through workshops and then transform it into public performances, forming a healing path "from private to public". In addition, "time-limited creation rules" (such as 48 hours to complete the script) are used to stimulate creative potential.
Public participation: from audience to "co-performers"
Through the "recruit-generate" model, p4 transforms viewers into creators. For example, "The Howler on the Rooftop" had lines co-written by participants, while "Iceberg" recorded a collective debate triggered by the "Rose Incident". This "decentralized" model challenges the authoritative structure of traditional theater and enables art to become a medium for social dialogue.
4. Social Impact and Controversy
Experimental sample of art democratization
P4 Theater By lowering the threshold for participation, it attracts a large number of non-professional artists and the general public. Its projects have incubated a number of independent art groups, such as "Beifeng Theater Society", "Glass Theater Troupe", etc., forming a "fission-type" ecology. The audience commented that his work "can see the life state behind the non-professional actors", highlighting the concern for "the courage of human existence".
Controversy: The tension between eliteness and popularity
Despite its emphasis on publicity, p4's practices are still questioned for "over-reliance on the founder's personal philosophy." For example, its psychoanalysis-oriented methodology is considered "academic elitist", while improvisational rules can lead to creative fragmentation. In addition, some experimental works (such as "Final Solution") have caused social controversy because they involve sensitive issues.
5. Conclusion: The future of theater as a "social hard drive"
P4 Theater's ten years of practice have reconstructed the definition of theater: it is not only an art exhibition space, but also a "hard disk engraved with life." Through interdisciplinary collaboration, rule innovation and social participation, its exploration provides the following enlightenment for contemporary art
art as connector
Break individual loneliness and build an emotional community
Rules as productivity
Inspire creative possibilities through methodological design
failure as nourishment
Approaching reality and freedom through trial and error.
In the future, P4 Theater may need to further balance experimentation and sustainability, but its core spirit-finding light in the darkness, asking for truth in performance-will remain an important reference for China's independent art ecology.

P4 Theater, Ten Years
A ten-year P4 Theater archive connecting Real Image, The Last Rehearsal, Human Surrender, AGT, recruitment, and live-site practice.
P4 Theater began in its founder's obsession with how to capture what is true. Theater became a container; photography became a method for inscribing real existence. From the early photographic practice of Real Image to the eventual filming of Human Surrender, P4 has repeatedly called that dense, irreducible, repressed Real onto the stage, then engraved its exposure record into digital negatives.
From the first construction of P4 Theater in 2015 to the move from Tiantongyuan to the Wanghualu office in 2021, P4 went through repeated rises and falls. Its concepts, consciousness, and attitudes kept adjusting and changing through practice.

P4 has held more than a hundred workshops of all sizes. People filled each space with love. We can become what we want to become: free, not defined by others, becoming.
Ten years of P4 Theater were formed by the visits of tens of thousands of people. Without these friends, the name would be an empty tower. With our own actions we built a passage toward the impossible: toward love, loss, pain, and all the reasons that force us to keep living.
Recording is the reason P4 Theater exists. We have recorded almost every story that happened in the theater: the nervous anticipation when people first entered, the red-faced arguments during rehearsal, the laughter, revelry, and tears after performances. Theater happens not only onstage, but also offstage.
P4 turns the camera into a ghost: wandering, then freezing the instant when lives collide.
The trinity of film, theater, and documentary is P4's final direction. In the practice of Human Surrender, truth and fiction begin to blur and leap out of place; actor, role, and desire begin to intertwine and copulate; the cinematographer is no longer a third-party observer, and the relation between watching and performing has already shattered the position of the object through repeated distancing. I call this impasse cinema: an emotional tremor that must be faced at close range, a reality beneath theatrical performance, a simple, plain, pure presentation, a release under absolute trust. This is also what P4 Theater has taught me over these years, through rehearsal after rehearsal: the truest thing.
In ten years I went from twenty-five to thirty-five. Because of theater, my life was placed on a roller coaster that rose to the sky and plunged underground: tossed, spun, sunk, released. It forced me from an INTP into an ENFP; I began to learn to cry, to roar, to become hysterical, to speak bravely. Real life is filled with predicaments that demand compromise or escape. Perhaps if they are placed inside a play, even the fate that embarrasses me can have its moment of highlight. I long for these fragments of image to be witnessed in the future.

2024-11-07
Theory and Methods
p4 Contribution｜Poetics of Fangs: Preliminary Explanation of Dark Conceptual Theory｜Jacob Reber
Staring absentmindedly at the inhuman fluorescent screen |||||||||||||The absent-minded fear turned into inhuman screams
We are the poets of your nightmares, feeding on the fleshy documents-spreading and infusing death into the text.
Looking blankly at the inhuman fluorescent screen
The absent-minded fear turned into inhuman screams
The poet labors in silence, summoning the unknown onto the paper through monastic rituals. Transcribe text alone. Some may seek to summon inhuman spiritual forces, others to machine-like inhumanity-yet both spread noise, chaos, and the unknown that already exists.
The collapse of the occult and digital technology occurs through the interface - "high-speed digital technology sweeps the imagination of those who are fascinated by it, suggestively tampering with our senses, and attracting our interconnected minds."
Connections to the outside are always risky, open to something new but irrevocable. This potential and becoming space is also a risk and omen. The Bard of Fangs opens with a call, creating a passage into the unknown.
Only the soft glow of the screen caresses the fanged poet's face - he is surrounded by unknown darkness, waiting. Then write, lead, infect the page-the piercing wound that ends each sentence, dots each i, and leads into a new phrase.
.. i i!!
Fang Bards are not necessarily entirely human - they are mythical, animal, cyborg, prophetic, divine, etc. Fang Bards are "dangerous, cruel aliens" who are often positioned as "evil outsiders." They come from elsewhere, pouring in from the margins of the human cluster, permeating different material planes, emphasizing the immateriality inherent in matter. Materiality is not denied but revealed as a destroyed world of textual sludge.
Instead of working for humanity, they invite the possibility of destruction. Unconsciously accelerating darkness.
Fang Bards imitate humans using retractable tusks and cunning camouflage or refraction techniques. The fanged poet is not a vampire, but more like a poisonous snake - less temptation, more venom.
"I'm not
Serve humanity. "
The fangs work very subtly-they don't chop, they pierce, working under the cover of the mouth-without anyone noticing.
The Fang Bard creates traps and places himself in them. Their hands are always stained with blood-"and even worse, there's the illusion that it might be pure, which excuses it."
This is not an evil poetics, but an examination of the work. It tries to cast its gaze downwards, trying to exist in a space of complicity. This messy ambivalence, covered in blood, does not know where it comes from.
To reach out is to enter the horror, to channel the inhuman horror that already exists-we just don't want to open our eyes.
In "Shamanic Nietszche," Nick Land describes Nietzsche as "a fanged poet at war with the philosopher." Our research interest is in what it means to actually be a fang poet-to develop a fang poetics.
Through this text, a series of eight characteristics/rules/mysteries can be summoned
Brief description
[The Fang Bard rarely reveals himself-usually hiding in lightless rooms, dirty machines, feedback loops, dank caves... non-places. Fang Bards are never singular, they are always proliferating rapidly - this list covers any Fang Bard, but it is still incomplete - it reveals little about the Fang Bards' material, if such a thing exists. ]
Fang Bard //////In 8 Catastrophic Fragments //////
1| The fang poet makes life into problems
2| On the side of ideas, against knowledge
3| Operation through luck
4| Intrusion, not expression
5| Heading towards the unknown
6| Immoral // (Immortal)
7| The fang poet makes poetry look ferocious
8| Breeding, Penetration and Destruction
Fang poet makes life problematic
"Describing and praising life
Poetry takes pleasure in death. "
The poet disturbs thought, making distinctions more difficult, always looking for para-sites, disrupting clear breaks between locations - steeping himself in contradictions and ambiguities.
Poetry is often dismissed as beautiful prose. Inhabiting the flowery words, gliding across the page in clean, brief lines. It focuses the eye on flowers - parodying their symmetry, beautiful text, soft petals. The fang poem reminds us of thorns.
Fang poetry is far removed from known emotions, truths, images, etc. It complicates and brings the poem together. The job of the Fang Bard is to superimpose and reconfigure. Reconstructed and reconsidered - "poetry is depicted as a fragmented visual derangement and a disorder of the self".
On the side of ideas, against knowledge
"Poetry is not the knowledge of oneself, nor the experience of distant possibilities (things that did not exist before), but the simple reproduction of unreachable possibilities through words."
Conceptual fangs interest not the reader but the thinker
To read a conceptual text is to immerse yourself in the horrors of technocapitalism. All kinds of surrounding texts, stupid nonsense, stolen words and unconscious copying can be found in the reading process. Thinking is not a means of escape but a way of parsing the horror, a way of getting caught up in it, a way of expanding and recirculating the material. Reading is individual processing, while thinking is downloading and copying the dark conceptual plague.
The fang poet is not creating, but rearranging, copying and reorganizing. This is a process of mobility and connectivity. We think and inhabit dark mental spaces, evoking riots on the page.
The only knowledge the poet is interested in is its absence - "What if knowledge is a means of exacerbating the unknown?" It is a path to destruction - "The logic within a work or series of works is a strategy that sometimes works but will eventually be destroyed."
Operate by chance
The fang poet does not know the possibilities that each text holds. The words are often motionless-always at a standstill, always at rest. But these words have the potential to decompose-to become sites of death. This violent form of becoming is always a threat.
The Fang Poet's poetry does not create new knowledge, nor does it solidify-it is fluid: "It is not a concept that needs to be understood, but a direction forward." It is a practice of Oulipian chance operations.
Queneau's sonnet creates an impossible task for the reader - a compressed file that will crash the brain of the reader who tries and becomes obsessed with understanding.
"All ten sonnets have the same rhyme pattern and use the same rhymes. Therefore, any line in one sonnet can be combined with any line in the other nine sonnets, resulting in 10^14 (= 100,000,000,000,000) different poems. Reading them twenty-four hours a day would take you approximately 140,000,000 years to read them all."
Not only is this impossible, but the endless reorganization is constantly producing new content, resulting in texts that may have never been read before. Each sonnet is a command with unknown consequences-infinite consequences in every encounter.
Intrusion, not expression
Lyrical poetry and fang poets are not compatible. It's boring, self-indulgent, and inconsequential.
"This anthology is not about natural expression, personal style, or the rhetoric of voice, but rather about a set of cold procedures. It is not about psychological development or dramatic narrative, but detailed logical extrapolation or permutation."
The poet must always assert and declare that everything is poetry. Although this totalizing gesture has its shortcomings, it attempts to incorporate the outside and/or the unknown into every utterance.
In 1919, after Gabriele D'Annunzio "seized the disputed territory of the city of Fiume," the artists, after a Duchampian nomination, declared Fiume officially a nation-state. This unmitigated invasion interprets part of the fanged poet's work, materializing an impossible poetic space. As Bataille said, the fang poet creates "impossible possibilities."
"Violence is not going away, whether it's psychological or physical, it's very practical in many ways. Given that violence is one of our instincts, how do we dispatch it?"
Toward the unknown
